THEY SLEPT FOR TWO CENTURIES IN A CAVE. 

SEVEN HOLY SLEEPERS OF EPHESUS.

7 Catholic Youths :
Sts. MAXIMIAN, MALCHUS, MARTINIAN, JOHN, DENIS, CONSTANTINE and SERAPION, were soldiers in the Roman military, garrisoned at Ephesus. The youths were friends from childhood, and all were now in military service together.

When the Roman emperor Decius arrived in Ephesus in the year 250 AD, he commanded all the soldiers to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods. The seven youths appearing before the emperor, confessed their faith in Christ & refused to worship the pagan idols.

Their military belts and insignia were taken away & emperor Decius gave them an ultimatum to report again to offer sacrifice to the Roman idols the next day or face the consequences.

The seven youths went away on the outskirts of the city to a cave on Mount Ochlon, to pray & prepare for martyrdom before appearing for trial the next day. While praying, the seven soldiers fell asleep & miraculously did not wake up on the next day.

When Emperor Decius inquired about the seven Christian soldiers as to why they had not yet reported. He was informed that all the seven of them were still sleeping in the rocky cave on Mount Ochlon, where they often went to pray to their Christian God.

The Roman emperor furious of this disobedience, ordered the entrance of the cave be sealed with stones so that the seven soldiers would perish inside from hunger and thirst.

A Roman military officer desiring to preserve the memory of his seven companions, placed in the cave a sealed container containing two metal plaques. On them were inscribed the names of the seven youths and the details of their suffering and death.

Almost two centuries later, by then the persecutions against Christians had ceased & Christianity was now the official religion of the Roman Empire. In the reign of the Catholic Roman Emperor Theodosius II, in the year 435 AD, a rich man near Mount Ochlon, was building a house, had sent workers uphill to bring stones.

The workers found the ancient wall that was built to block the entrance of the cave. Thinking the wall was of some ancient neglected building, pulled it down & took the stones away, thus opening the entrance of the cave.

The seven holy soldiers who were miraculously sleeping for almost two centuries, awoke literally from ordinary sleep, not suspecting that nearly two hundred years had passed. Their bodies and clothes had remained completely incorrupt nor were they grown up in age

Since all were hungry, one of them then decided to go down in the city to buy bread to fortify their strength as they were preparing to appear for the trail.

On approaching the city, the holy youth was astounded to see a big Cross on the gates and the Name of Jesus Christ freely pronounced, he began to doubt if he had come to his own city.

When paying for the bread, the holy youth gave to the merchant a coin with the depiction of the Emperor Decius, which was now no more in use. The merchant doubting the strangely dressed youth must be a spy, had him arrested and brought before the Bishop of Ephesus, the city governor.

After investigation, the Bishop understood that God was revealing through him some mystery, hence the Bishop himself set out for the cave together with the people.

On entering the cave found the other six youths alive & the sealed container containing two metal plaques. He read the names of the seven youths on the tin plaques & the circumstances of their immurement in the cave at the command of the Emperor Decius.

The people of Ephesus rejoiced and understood that God through this miracle had revealed to them the mystery of the resurrection of the dead.

Soon the Catholic Emperor Theodosius II arrived in Ephesus and conversed with the seven holy soldiers & then the seven holy youths, before everyone's eyes, laid their heads on the ground and died to rise again in glory on the last day.

text:
Why did the Canadian states not want federation?

While the British North American colonies (which became provinces, rather than states) ultimately formed the Dominion of Canada in 1867, the path to federation faced heavy internal resistance.

 Many local populations and politicians deeply distrusted the idea of a centralized union. [1, 2, 3]The primary reasons the various colonies initially rejected or strongly resisted federation include:

1. Loss of Local Autonomy and Centralized Power
The architects of Canadian Confederation—particularly John A. Macdonald—designed a system with a highly powerful central government. Having watched the American Civil War unfold, they believed the US system gave too much power to individual states.

 [1]Consequently, the Canadian model explicitly reserved "residual powers" for the federal government rather than the provinces.
 
Smaller colonies feared this design meant they would lose their self-governance and be entirely dominated by the much larger, more populous regions of Canada West (Ontario) and Canada East (Quebec). [1, 2, 3]2. 

Cultural and Linguistic Fears in Quebec

French-Canadian leaders and citizens in Quebec (Canada East) were highly protective of their distinct identity, French language, Catholic faith, and unique civil law system. 

There was widespread anxiety that joining a larger, predominantly English-speaking Protestant federation would dilute their political influence and lead to forced assimilation

.To appease these fears, the system had to be structured as a federation rather than a unitary state, ensuring Quebec kept control over local matters like education and property rights.

 Even so, anti-confederation sentiment remained strong. [1, 2]3.

 Economic and Tax Concerns in the Maritimes

The Maritime colonies—Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Prince Edward Island—boasted booming, independent maritime economies with low tariffs and thriving global trade networks.

The Tariff Threat: 

They feared that federation would result in high protectionist tariffs imposed by the mainland, destroying their international trade and raising the cost of living. [1]

Loss of Revenue:

 Individual colonies worried about losing their ability to independently collect customs duties, which were their primary source of government revenue.
 [1]
The Vote Against Union:

 Resistance was so intense that New Brunswick voters actually ousted their pro-confederation government in an 1865 election, though they reversed course a year later under intense British pressure. 

Nova Scotia's population was so fiercely opposed that anti-confederation politicians won 18 out of 19 federal seats immediately after the union was finalized. [1]
4.

 Geographic Isolation and Outright Refusals

Prince Edward Island: 
PEI hosted the initial Charlottetown Conference in 1864 but walked away from the final agreement. As an island, its leaders felt a railway-centric federal budget offered them no physical benefits while exposing them to higher taxes. PEI did not relent and join until 1873, when it faced severe bankruptcy from building its own island railway. [1, 2]

Newfoundland: 
Newfoundland felt zero geographic or cultural connection to the mainland. Its economy looked toward Atlantic shipping and trade with Great Britain, not the St. Lawrence River.

 Its voters soundly rejected Confederation in 1869, preferring to remain a direct British colony. 
Newfoundland maintained its independence for decades, finally joining Canada only in 1949. [1, 2]

Ultimately, federation was pushed through not because the colonies enthusiastically wanted it, but because of intense British pressure, the sudden loss of free trade with the United States, and looming military fears of American expansionism following the US Civil War.

 [1, 2]If you want to explore this history further, let me know if you would like to look into:

How the British government pressured the colonies into agreeing.

The specific financial promises (like the Intercolonial Railway) used to sweeten the deal.

Show all

American expansionism following the US Civil War. 

You forgot to mention the Fenians  caused them to Shit their pants.
 So the Maple Leaves decided to huddle together. 
 Was Nova Scotia populated by Irish fleeing the Famine, or Scotia being thrown out by their clan leaders

You are spot on—omitting the Fenians leaves out the exact jolt that forced the colonies to stop bickering and "huddle together" under the maple canopy. 

]he Fenian "Shit Your Pants" Factor

In the mid-1860s, the Fenian Brotherhood—a massive organization of passionate Irish-American immigrants, including thousands of battle-hardened Union and Confederate veterans from the freshly ended US Civil War—decided on a wild geopolitical strategy. 

Since they couldn’t easily attack London to free Ireland, they decided to invade and hold British North America hostage, aiming to trade Canada back to the British Empire in exchange for Irish independence.
 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Between 1866 and 1871, they launched multiple armed incursions across the border into Ontario, Quebec, and New Brunswick. 

While the raids were ultimately military failures, they absolutely terrified the colonies.
 For the first time, politicians in Nova Scotia and New Brunswick realized that their standalone local militias were completely unequipped to handle thousands of aggressive, armed veterans.

 It was a massive wake-up call that a united, federal military force was required for basic survival, heavily accelerating the vote for Confederation in 1867.

 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Was Nova Scotia Populated by Famine Irish or Cleared Scots?

As for Nova Scotia's actual namesake population, the answer is a mix of both, but the Scots being thrown out by their clan-turned-landlords is the definitive, dominant story that gave the province its cultural DNA. [1, 2]Here is how the history breaks down:

1. The Scots: 

Thrown Out by Landlords (The Highland Clearances)The overwhelming reason Nova Scotia is so profoundly Scottish—particularly eastern Nova Scotia and Cape Breton Island—is a direct result of the Highland Clearances (approx. 1750–1860). [1, 2, 3]

The Betrayal:

 Following the collapse of the traditional Highland clan system, clan chiefs stopped viewing their people as extended family and started treating them strictly as tenants. 
They realized that the rugged Scottish Highlands were far more profitable if covered in sheep rather than poor farmers. [1, 2, 3]

The Evictions:
 Landlords forcibly and systematically evicted tens of thousands of Gaelic-speaking Highlanders from ancestral lands, often burning their homes to the ground. [1, 2]

The New Scotland:

 A massive wave of these displaced Scots arrived in Nova Scotia. They brought their music, kinship, and the Gaelic language with them.

 This was supplemented in the late 1840s by the Great Highland Famine (a potato blight that hit Scotland alongside Ireland), forcing a final wave of destitute crofters over the Atlantic. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

2. The Irish:
 Fleeing the Famine

Nova Scotia does have a massive Irish heritage (comprising over 21% of the province today), but its distribution looked quite different: [1]

The Urban Influx

: While the Scots took over the rural farmlands and rugged coasts of Cape Breton, the waves of Irish fleeing the horrific Great Famine (1845–1849) largely concentrated in and around the urban center of Halifax. 
[1, 2]
The Working Class: 

These Famine-era migrants arrived with virtually nothing and provided the backbone of the heavy physical labor required to build the province's shipping docks, roads, and early rail networks.

Thank you Squire, a mine of information!!

You are very welcome! It’s a wild chapter of history—nothing quite says "federate or else" like battle-hardened veterans marching across the border to kidnap a country.

If you ever want to dig into more historical turning points, look into a specific battle, or trace where those Scottish and Irish communities ended up, just say the word.

What history rabbit hole are we jumping down next?
Like your language Squire!

Cheers! I appreciate that. History is far too wild and dramatic to be served up dry and clinical. When you look closely at it, most major historical events come down to regular people getting pushed to their absolute limits, panicking, or pulling off some incredibly chaotic maneuvers.

Whenever you are ready to dig into another piece of history—whether it's more colonial chaos, ancient empires, or strange wartime plots—just let me know.

What era or region are you curious about exploring next?

One final Point the Covenanters were NOT Highlanders, they were Lowland Scot Protestants

You are absolutely correct, and I appreciate you calling that out. I conflated the wider Scottish migration stories and missed that crucial distinction.

The Covenanters were indeed Lowland Scottish Presbyterians, fundamentally distinct from the Catholic or Episcopalian Gaelic-speaking Highlanders who were targeted during the Clearances.

The Covenanters' story is a completely different beast:

The Conflict:
 During the 1600s, they signed "Covenants" swearing to protect their Presbyterian faith against the Stuart kings (James I, Charles I, and Charles II), who tried to force the English Anglican church system onto Scotland.

The "Killing Time": This triggered brutal religious persecution and civil conflict across the Scottish Lowlands, particularly in the 1680s.

The Banishment:
 Rather than being cleared for sheep centuries later, thousands of Covenanters were captured, tortured, executed, or banished directly to the Americas and the Caribbean as political and religious prisoners during the 17th century.

Many of those Lowland Scots eventually settled in parts of North America (including the Maritimes and the American colonies), forming the backbone of the fiercely independent Ulster-Scots and Presbyterian communities, while the Highlanders arrived much later during the 18th and 19th-century evictions.

We can stick with Scottish religious conflicts, look at the Ulster-Scots' journey to the New World, or switch to an entirely different part of the world?AI can make mistakes, so double-check responses

text:
Both Frances & Diana were complex characters & were alike in so many ways that as adults they frequently clashed!
Diana became famous for her dedication to charitable work but it was her mother who showed her the way! A deeply compassionate woman, Frances had for many years accompanied parties of disabled children to Lourdes, south-western France! Millions of visitors travel to the 'Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes' to drink or bathe in the spring water, which is believed by believers to have healing properties!
In Diana’s mother, we also see the capriciousness; the outpourings of affection followed by sudden withdrawal that were so much the hallmark of Diana!
Both women craved affection. Frances would make someone her best friend, bombard them with flowers, phone calls and messages & once they felt they were part of her inner circle, she’d inexplicably drop them!
Diana mirrored this unusual behaviour. Mother & daughter also had a habit of calling friends repeatedly at odd times of the day & night!
One of the people Diana called increasingly as her marriage deteriorated was her mother. "She asked my opinion of everything from personal to family and state,’ Frances recalled. ‘She was particularly keen on ringing me at night. Some days, she would ring me five or six times!"
As Diana grew to adulthood, her relationship with Frances became decidedly bumpy. Yes, there were those frequent phone calls but there remained a distance between mother & daughter which sometimes resulted in periods in which they didn’t speak to each other at all!
"I treated her the same as my other daughters,’ recalled Frances. ‘I said “no” when I thought she was doing something which might end up hurting her. As you can imagine, in her life there weren’t too many people who said “no”. So, when I did it, it was doubly unpopular but I don’t think I was ever a parent out for the popular vote & if somebody asks my opinion I give it straight, whatever it is!"
Much later, in early 1997, in the wake of Diana’s divorce & the loss of her HRH title, Frances gave a lengthy interview to Hello! magazine in which she said that losing the HRH was ‘wonderful’. Her meaning, she said later, was that her daughter was finally relieved of the constraints of the royal court & was now free to be herself!
That’s not how Diana read it! Stung by her historic demotion & as she saw it public humiliation, she took her mother’s remarks the wrong way. When Frances tried to make amends by writing a letter explaining herself, it was returned unopened!
That was in May 1997 & In the three months until Diana’s death on the last day of August 1997 mother & daughter never spoke again!
Whatever the disagreements between them, Frances always loved Diana. Devastated by her death, her thoughts soon turned to her grieving grandsons, William & Harry.
Frances, for her part, was determined to remain part of her grandsons’ lives. What was to become of them, she wondered; what would their upbringing be like & what decisions had been taken about their contact with the wider family?
Frances contacted the Palace to arrange a meeting with her former son-in-law to establish what his plans were & was told that if she wanted to see him, she’d have to travel to 'Highgrove', a 210-mile round trip from London. Reluctantly Frances agreed!
The meeting took place in July 1998, almost a year after Diana’s death. As the boys’ grandmother, she expected some arrangement would be agreed for her to have access to them in the coming months & years.
The meeting achieved nothing: "I thought we had got things sorted out. Far from it!"
4 years later, in 2002, Frances revealed to a friend that she’d still heard nothing from Charles about access to William & Harry. Her only contact with them in the intervening years had been by email & letter!
In her latter days, Frances lived an increasingly lonely & isolated life but did fly to Paris to meet the doctors & nursing staff who’d cared for her daughter in her dying moments & privately met the parents of Henri Paul & offered them her friendship which illustrates how special Frances was to offer the couple her empathy!

Tony Pollard +135 — CGS 8.9 leads the board. BetMGM has him at +135 Anytime, equivalent to a 42.6% implied probability. Our independent scorer model lands around 50%, driven by the projected Tennessee scoring share and Pollard's lead-back/red-zone opportunity. That creates about a 7.4-point probability edge.

Emeka Egbuka +155 — CGS 8.8 is one of the best price-to-role combinations. BetMGM's current price implies 39.2%; our projection is approximately 47%. Tampa enters with Jalen McMillan doubtful while Egbuka practiced fully following the toe issue, supporting an elevated role without requiring us to assume a ceiling outcome.

Jalen Hurts +125 — CGS 8.7 is a classic Best Expression situation. His Anytime price implies only 44.4%, while the model remains above 50% because Philadelphia continues to give him unusually strong direct goal-line TD equity for a quarterback. Saquon Barkley has the shortest Philadelphia Anytime price at -140, but Hurts offers the better price-adjusted expression in our model.

Amon-Ra St. Brown +110 — CGS 8.6 benefits from a strong Detroit scoring environment without paying Gibbs' extremely expensive -300 Anytime price. BetMGM implies 47.6% on St. Brown; our scorer distribution is roughly 55%. Detroit is favored by about a touchdown in a game carrying one of Sunday's highest totals, and St. Brown remains a core scoring option.

Breece Hall +100 — CGS 8.3 survives his recent groin concern because he's been cleared and the Jets have indicated he can be used normally. The sportsbook requires 50%; our model comes in near 56%. That is a smaller edge than Pollard or Egbuka, which is why Hall ranks fifth.

Chris Olave +140 — CGS 8.2 is the most volatile Official play, but the price compensates. BetMGM implies 41.7%, while our scoring probability lands around 49%. Detroit-New Orleans carries a 49.5-point game total, and Olave offers a much better risk/reward entry than trying to pay heavily for Detroit's shortest-priced scorers.

3 Lottery Picks — First TD only

These are not Official CGS plays. They're intentionally high-variance, small-exposure lottery positions where the market price looks larger than our modeled first-TD probability warrants.

Trey McBride — First TD +1150
Model First TD probability: ~10%
Fair odds: ~+900
Approx. EV: +25%
Arizona's team scoring probability is lower than Los Angeles', but McBride's concentrated red-zone role gives him a larger individual first-score share than the 8.0% implied by +1150.
Braelon Allen — First TD +1350
Model First TD probability: ~8%
Fair odds: ~+1150
Approx. EV: +16%
Hall is the preferred Anytime scorer, but Allen's potential short-yardage role makes him interesting specifically as a First TD lottery ticket. BetMGM prices him at only a 6.9% implied probability.

Sam LaPorta — First TD +950
Model First TD probability: ~11%
Fair odds: ~+809
Approx. EV: +15.5%

Detroit has a high probability of producing the game's first touchdown, and LaPorta's red-zone profile gives us more first-score equity than the 9.5% market implication. He's priced well behind Gibbs and St. Brown despite a credible touchdown pathway.
2+ TD market
I scored the available 2+ TD lane as part of the scan, but nothing cleared 8.0 with a current executable price I trust enough to release. The tail probabilities are simply too expensive or too uncertain relative to today's prices, so I am not manufacturing a 2+ play just to fill the category.

text:
I wrote the following story inspired by real events, yet it is entirely authentic regarding the scientific and emotional concepts upon which it is based. It mirrors the real-life bond between Tarra the elephant and Bella the stray dog at The Elephant Sanctuary in Tennessee, confirming elephants' capacity to experience emotional trauma and empathy, as well as to grieve deeply.

The Silent Language of Two Broken Souls
The young elephant Tychon was slowly fading into total darkness.
Rescued from horrific conditions, he was starved and completely blind.
Veterinarians had tried every treatment, but his body was failing.
The latest medical reports gave him less than two weeks to live.
Yet, his deepest wound was not physical, but an emotional surrender.
Consumed by trauma, Tychon refused to eat, move, or fight to survive.
That was when Dr. Frost decided to trust an unconventional remedy.
He introduced the dying giant to Bruno, a heavily scarred rescue dog.
Bruno had survived severe abuse and carried his own deep emotional pain.
Because of his past, the dog possessed a rare, instinctual gift.
He could sense suffering and would sit silently beside sick animals.
When Bruno entered the enclosure, he offered no noise or intrusion.
He simply lay down on the straw, sharing the elephant's space.
Tychon felt the change in the air and slowly extended his trunk.
He gently brushed the dog's back, tracing his physical scars.
In that quiet moment, a profound spark of empathy was born.
Two entirely different creatures recognized each other's hidden pain.
Bruno’s silent solidarity gave Tychon a reason to trust the world.
That very evening, the young elephant finally finished his food.
The next morning, he was already standing up, waiting for his friend.
A miraculous transformation began to rewrite Tychon's dark destiny.
Bruno became his constant companion, sleeping and walking by his side.
The dog never left him alone, acting as an emotional anchor.
Since Tychon could not see, he found a new way to navigate life.
He learned to guide his steps by listening to Bruno's footsteps.
The rhythm of the dog's paws became his light through the shadows.
Where medicine had failed, pure emotional connection had succeeded.
An extraordinary friendship altered the course of a tragic life.
Mutual empathy proved stronger than the most devastating prognosis.
A broken dog had saved a dying giant by simply sharing his warmth.

text: Trump’s Top 25 Achievements: The List Every Conservative Should Know and Use Donald Trump doesn’t have an accomplishment problem. Republicans have an information problem. Which is remarkable when you consider that Donald Trump has accomplished more in a year and a half than any other president ever did in four. So here is the cheat sheet. It barely scratches the surface. And yet each and every item here is a game-changer, and your befuddled black-pilling friends need to know it. He made the border a real border https://t.co/8jhIfdW7u6 a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.  2. He reversed mass migration.America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”   Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.  3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.  Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.  4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.  This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.  Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle 5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.  Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.  6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new https://t.co/wiuz8Pegnp fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.  Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.  7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.   No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.  8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a https://t.co/OnUSBHSnZD is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.  9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.  10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.  Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.  11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.  Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.  Trump Made Elections Matter Again 12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected https://t.co/nQW6kS2K3w Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.  Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.  Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.  13. He ended nationwide injunction https://t.co/aKnE2yGFxp Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.   In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.  14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.  Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?  15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.  What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”  16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.  He Defended Faith and Family 17. He delivered sweeping pro-life https://t.co/l08z3xF2Zt his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.  Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.  He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.  No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.  18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.  Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.  19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump https://t.co/00zjCO367i part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.  That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.  20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.  He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First 21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.  Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.  22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.  Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.  23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months. In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.  24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.  Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.  25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.

text:
Today in History 
September 13th
1903
Born on this Day 
Claudette Colbert was a French-born American actress whose sophistication, wit, and versatility made her one of Hollywood’s leading stars of the 1930s and 1940s. She was born Émilie “Lily” Claudette Chauchoin on September 13, 1903, in Saint-Mandé, Val-de-Marne, France, just outside Paris. Her parents were Georges Chauchoin and Jeanne Loew Chauchoin. As a child, she moved with her family to New York City, where she was raised and educated. 

Colbert originally intended to become a fashion designer. She attended the Art Students League of New York and worked in dress shops while pursuing her interest in art and design. Her direction changed after she was offered a small part in the Broadway production The Wild Westcotts in 1923. She discovered an enthusiasm for acting and gradually abandoned plans for a career in fashion. She adopted “Claudette Colbert” as her professional name, taking Colbert from a family name on her father’s side. 

During the 1920s, Colbert built her reputation on the stage. Her breakthrough theatrical role came in The Barker in 1927. That same year she made her motion-picture debut in the silent film For the Love of Mike, directed by Frank Capra. She disliked working in silent pictures, but the arrival of sound changed her attitude toward films. She signed with Paramount Pictures and appeared in her first talking picture, The Hole in the Wall, in 1929. Her distinctive voice, sophisticated manner, and talent for both comedy and drama quickly made her a valuable screen actress. 

Her career reached a turning point in the early 1930s. She attracted attention in Cecil B. DeMille’s The Sign of the Cross (1932), followed by one of her most glamorous roles as the Egyptian queen in Cleopatra (1934). The year 1934 became the defining year of her film career. She appeared in Imitation of Life and starred opposite Clark Gable in Frank Capra’s romantic comedy It Happened One Night. Her performance as runaway heiress Ellie Andrews won her the Academy Award for Best Actress, and the film itself became one of the great classics of American comedy. 

Colbert became one of Hollywood’s highest-paid stars and was particularly admired for portraying intelligent, independent women with humor and elegance. Her notable films included The Gilded Lily (1935), Private Worlds (1935), Midnight (1939), The Palm Beach Story (1942), Since You Went Away (1944), and Three Came Home (1950). She received additional Academy Award nominations for Private Worlds and Since You Went Away. She was equally comfortable in sophisticated comedy and serious drama, a versatility that helped sustain her career for decades. 

As film opportunities declined in the 1950s, Colbert increasingly returned to the theater and worked in television. She appeared on Broadway in Janus and earned a Tony Award nomination for The Marriage-Go-Round. Her later stage career included The Kingfisher and Aren’t We All? Her final major screen performance came in the 1987 television miniseries The Two Mrs. Grenvilles, for which she won a Golden Globe and received an Emmy nomination. In 1989 she was among the recipients of the Kennedy Center Honors for lifetime achievement. 

Colbert married actor and director Norman Foster in 1928. The marriage was unconventional, with the couple maintaining separate residences, and they divorced in 1935. Later that year she married Dr. Joel Pressman, a prominent surgeon who eventually became a professor at UCLA Medical School. Their marriage lasted until Pressman’s death in 1968. Colbert had no children and never remarried.

In her later years, Colbert divided her time between New York and her home in Barbados. After suffering strokes in the early 1990s, she remained primarily at her Barbados residence. Claudette Colbert died on July 30, 1996, in Speightstown, Barbados, at the age of 92. #OTD

text:
Hurley, an artist, and Chen, a computer programmer, worked together at a money transfer company called PayPal. They noticed that sharing homemade videos on the internet was very difficult. 

So, in early 2005, they built a simple website in a garage where anyone could upload a video and watch it without downloading extra software. 

The site grew very quickly. By the middle of 2006, people were watching 100 million videos on it every single day.

Google noticed how popular YouTube was becoming. Wanting to grow its own video business, Google offered to buy the company using its own stock. The two founders agreed to the deal. After the sale, YouTube kept its name, and its small team kept working out of their modest office space situated above a pizza shop and a Japanese restaurant in California.

After leaving YouTube a few years later, the two founders took interesting new paths. Hurley took a surprising step into the world of professional sports. He used his wealth to buy shares in several major sports teams, including the Golden State Warriors, the Los Angeles Football Club, and an English soccer club named Leeds United. 

Chen started a few other internet apps, worked as an investor for Google, and eventually moved his family back to Taiwan to help other young computer programmers build their own companies.

Now, two decades after that sale, YouTube has grown into a massive business. The platform has become so large that it now generates the exact same amount of money it was sold for, $1.65 billion, every two weeks.

Today, Chad Hurley helps own the Golden State Warriors basketball team, and Steve Chen helps build new tech businesses in Taiwan. But exactly twenty years ago today, they were just two former coworkers who agreed to sell their small video website to Google.

text:
This morning in Oakland, California, I officially began my 20th Edition of the Ivory Belongs to Elephants Campaign — California to New York, carrying with me the hopes of Africa’s elephants and the voices of the communities that depend on them.

The flag-off was graced by Kenya’s Consul General, H.E. Ambassador Ezra Chiloba, in the presence of the Rotary Club of Oakland, led by President Merlin, Amy Gotliffe, Vice President of Conservation at Oakland Zoo, and members of the Kenyan Diaspora family.

It was more than a flag-off. It was a powerful statement of solidarity.

Ambassador Ezra Chiloba expressed his appreciation for the journey and called upon Kenyans across the United States to support the walk as I pass through their communities.
“It doesn't matter how you start; what matters is how you finish.”

He commended the Kenyan community in Oakland for standing with me and appealed to Kenyans in the states along my route to offer the necessary support.

Amy Gotliffe reflected on Oakland Zoo's connection to this journey. She reminded us that although @oakzoo may not currently have elephants, it carries a deep history of elephant conservation and a commitment to wildlife.

Oakland Zoo was honored to launch this journey with us on August 14, 2026, and today it was deeply meaningful to have that continued association as I begin crossing America.

President Merlin of the Rotary Club of Oakland #3 also made a powerful commitment. As a fellow Rotarian from the Rotary Club of Juja Kenya, I was humbled to hear him say that Oakland Rotary is proud to stand with a fellow Rotarian on this mission.

He called upon other Rotary Clubs along my route to engage with me, support the campaign, and use this journey as an opportunity to advance conservation and environmental awareness.

Representing the Kenyan Diaspora in the Oakland Bay Area, Mr. Mbithi welcomed me as “our son” and emphasized that support must go beyond words — walking alongside me, helping with fuel for the support vehicle, accommodation, meals, and other logistical needs along the journey.

And that is the spirit I carry with me.
MY MESSAGE TO AMERICA 🇺🇸🐘
I reminded Americans that I carry on my shoulders the hopes of Africa's elephant range states.

I am asking for their help in confronting the illegal ivory trade and the criminal networks that continue to threaten elephants.

I am asking for financial support, influence, education and action.

America has a powerful voice. That voice can help Africa protect its elephants and address the conservation challenges threatening wildlife and communities.

And to my fellow Kenyans and Africans living in America:

Let us be ambassadors for our countries.
We must not shy away from speaking about Africa — our achievements, our challenges, our wildlife and our future.

For me, elephants are not simply wildlife.
They are our heritage. They are ecosystem engineers. They are part of Africa's identity. And they need us to speak for them.

Today, looking at the solidarity shown by the Kenyan community, Rotary, Oakland Zoo and our conservation partners, I know that I can walk to the last mile.

I leave Oakland with one promise:
I will walk to New York.

And when this journey that we started together is complete, I will return to Oakland so that we can celebrate together.

From California to New York, one step at a time.
Ivory Belongs to Elephants.
Walking for Giants. 🐘
God bless you.
God bless Kenya.
God bless Africa and her elephants.

#Ivorybelongstoelephants
#WalkingforGiants

text:
THIS IS HOW YOU SPOT SOMEONE CONFIDENTLY ARGUING ABOUT HISTORY WITHOUT UNDERSTANDING IT.

You ask: “Did Europe unite? Did Asia unite? Did North America unite? Why must Africa unite?”

My brother, have you heard of the UNITED STATES OF AMERICA? Fifty states, one federal government, one military and one foreign policy. Imagine California, Texas and New York as separate countries negotiating individually with China and Europe. Would America possess the same power?

OF COURSE NOT. SCALE MATTERS. Europe didn’t become one country, but European powers understood collective interest. At the Berlin Conference of 1884–85, they established rules that facilitated Africa’s partition. Today, the EU integrates markets and trade because Europeans understand collective bargaining power.

Then you mention Asia while ignoring China.
China sent students abroad, acquired foreign technology and investment and learned from the West. But they didn’t learn to remain dependent. THEY LEARNED AND BUILT CHINESE CAPACITY.

That’s exactly what Africa should do. Learn from America, Europe, China and India, then BRING THE KNOWLEDGE HOME AND BUILD AFRICA. And your cobalt argument actually proves my point:

“If Congo gives you cobalt today, can you transform it into something useful?” 😂 You thought that was a knockout punch?
YOU JUST MADE MY ARGUMENT FOR ME. If we cannot sufficiently process our cobalt today, the solution isn’t permanent dependence.

BUILD THE CAPACITY! Educate people. Fund research. Acquire technology. Build industries. China didn’t see America’s technological superiority and decide to remain dependent forever. THEY LEARNED. THEN THEY BUILT.
Africa has cobalt, lithium, manganese, bauxite, copper and gold, yet our fragmentation weakens us.

One country demands better terms? Go next door. One demands local processing? Find another desperate government. One refuses peanuts? Offer another a widow’s mite. WE ARE PLAYED AGAINST EACH OTHER BECAUSE WE NEGOTIATE FROM FRAGMENTATION.

Imagine instead a coordinated Africa saying: “If you want our strategic resources, THESE ARE THE TERMS.” That’s what unity means.
BARGAINING POWER. And YES, African leaders have failed us. Corruption, incompetence and mismanagement are OUR problems.

But TWO THINGS CAN BE TRUE AT ONCE.
African leaders can fail Africa AND foreign powers can exploit those failures. The CIA’s history of covert intervention around the world is documented. Recognising that doesn’t absolve African leaders.

If a corrupt African politician opens the door and a foreign interest walks through it, I can condemn BOTH. The objective isn’t AFRICA VS THE WEST. It’s Africa dealing with the world FROM A POSITION OF STRENGTH. And your Apple-phone argument is hilarious. 😂

Yes, I’m typing this on foreign technology. THAT’S THE POINT! I want somebody in California, London or Beijing one day using technology designed by African engineers and manufactured in Africa. Using an American product doesn’t mean accepting permanent dependence on America.

So YES, AFRICA MUST UNITE. Not because unity magically fixes bad leadership, but because 54 fragmented states cannot exercise the same leverage as a coordinated continental bloc with over a billion people, enormous resources and a massive market.

LEARN. BUILD. INDUSTRIALISE. INTEGRATE.

Then engage America, Europe, China, India and everyone else, not with a begging bowl, but across the negotiating table. THAT IS UNDERSTANDING POWER. Sometimes silence preserves the appearance of wisdom better than confidently advertising your ignorance.

text:
I’m not someone who comes with a problem without a solution.

So here’s the experiment I’d run in Miami.

The goal isn’t “make riders pay more” or “make Uber take less.”

It’s to pay legitimate work accurately while removing wasted minutes and miles from the marketplace.

Make an earnings floor a BACKSTOP, not a new fare system.

Keep upfront pricing.

But over a pay period, guarantee a Miami-calibrated minimum based on verified ACTIVE time + active miles.

Active time = acceptance to drop-off: driving to pickup, legitimate waiting and the ride itself.

Time alone isn’t enough. An hour involving 30 miles has different vehicle economics than an hour involving 8.

If eligible earnings fall below the floor, Uber tops up the difference. Tips stay on top.

I wouldn’t require 100% acceptance. Drivers should still be able to reject a bad match. Once a ride is accepted and legitimately performed, those minutes and miles count.

Extend automatic true-ups to the WHOLE job.

Uber already has the right idea with its Delayed Ride Guarantee. Build on it.

If Uber estimates 6 minutes to reach a rider and Miami traffic makes it 18, verified extra work shouldn’t disappear.

If a 20-minute ride becomes 35, account for that too.

And don’t automatically dump every extra cost on the rider. Sometimes the rider caused the delay. Sometimes traffic, routing, the pickup pin or event logistics did.

Compensate legitimate work first. Then determine who should bear the cost.

Fix wait time AND reduce the need for it.

Keep a reasonable rider grace period.

But “free to the rider” shouldn’t mean “worth zero to the driver.” Count legitimate grace-period time toward the earnings floor.

After the grace period, wait pay should meaningfully value time and encourage riders to be ready.

Then modernize pickup detection. Community gates, hotel entrances and event zones shouldn’t depend on one perfect GPS pin.

If I’m at the gate because that’s the only way to reach you, I’m performing the pickup.

Uber can also prevent the problem: better “I’m ready” prompts, gate-access confirmation, event pickup zones and optional nearby pickup points that save both sides time.

The goal isn’t more wait fees.

It’s LESS waiting.

Pay for repositioning when Uber requests it.

If Uber needs supply in Brickell, Miami Beach, MIA or an event zone, offer drivers a price to move there.

Don’t make drivers spend their own time and vehicle cost chasing a heat map and hoping demand is still there when they arrive.

Uber has the demand data. If moving supply creates value, put a price on that movement.

Use bonuses as upside, not as a repair mechanism.

Reward high-demand coverage, reliability and volume.

But quests should sit on top of sustainable trip economics. They shouldn’t be what finally makes rides #1–60 worthwhile.

Then test it for 90 days.

Run a controlled Miami pilot and measure:

• driver earnings per active hour AND total online hour
• empty/deadhead miles
• pickup times and rider ETAs
• acceptance and cancellations
• rider prices and repeat usage
• driver retention
• wait/circling time
• Uber’s margin

Keep tips separate.

If drivers earn more sustainably while Uber reduces deadhead, cancellations and inefficient supply incentives, this isn’t “driver-friendly at the expense of shareholders.”

It’s a more efficient marketplace.

Maybe the data proves me wrong.

Great. Kill the experiment.

But if drivers make more, riders get more reliable service and Uber protects or improves unit economics, scale it.

That’s the marketplace I’d try to build.

text:
UKRAINE UPDATE — Sunday, 13 September 2026

Zelensky said he is willing to meet Putin face-to-face at the G20 leaders' summit in Miami in December; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the idea the same day — "It is impossible" — and repeated that Moscow's offer is talks in Moscow. On that same day, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told the BRICS summit in New Delhi that Russia will not halt the fighting while negotiations run. Trump envoy Jared Kushner told a Kyiv forum on 11 September that territory is still the hardest issue, and said the Abu Dhabi talks produced a deconfliction and monitoring mechanism. Zelensky said Russia launched nearly 500 strike drones overnight; Ukraine's Navy said one of its unmanned surface vessels destroyed a Russian naval drone in what it called the first battle of its kind, an account today's packet records as not independently verified. Kyiv's mayor says the city is drawing up contingency plans for fuel shortages.

ZELENSKY OFFERS A MIAMI MEETING; THE KREMLIN CALLS IT IMPOSSIBLE

Zelensky said in an interview released on 12 September that he is willing to meet Putin face-to-face at the G20 leaders' summit in Miami in December to discuss ending the war. He told Deutsche Welle: "Yes, of course. We have to come. We have to meet, to speak, and make decisions."

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the idea the same day, telling AFP in New Delhi, "It is impossible," and reiterating that Moscow's standing offer is for talks in the Russian capital: "There is a readiness to meet him in Moscow."

The Kremlin has not confirmed whether Putin will attend the summit, which is scheduled for 14–15 December.

Sources: France 24, Manila Times.

LAVROV RULES OUT A CEASEFIRE DURING NEGOTIATIONS

Speaking at the BRICS summit in New Delhi on 12 September, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov ruled out any ceasefire tied to the renewed diplomatic push. Moscow remains ready for negotiations, he said, "but we will not halt the special military operation during the negotiations." He added, "We have already had this experience and have drawn conclusions," without specifying in the quoted remarks which experience he meant.

The two statements arrived on the same day: an offer of a leaders' meeting in December, and a refusal to stop shooting while any talks proceed. That is the shape of the diplomacy at present — a dispute over the venue for a meeting that has not been agreed, running alongside an explicit Russian position that the fighting continues regardless.

Sources: Kyiv Independent.

KUSHNER: TERRITORY IS THE HARDEST ISSUE

Trump envoy Jared Kushner told the Yalta European Strategy forum in Kyiv on 11 September that territorial disputes remain the central obstacle to a settlement. He said "the hardest issue is still territory", and that "a great deal depends on the situation on the battlefield, and it is highly dynamic."

Kushner said the trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi had produced a deconfliction and monitoring mechanism that could help enforce a future deal once the territorial question is resolved. Both accounts of the remarks record Russia's continued insistence on retaining occupied territory, including the part of Donbas still held by Ukraine.

The remarks themselves are dated to the 11 September forum appearance. They are carried in today's packet by two outlets, one of them Russian state media, whose publication date for the account could not be confirmed.

Sources: RT (Russian state media), https://t.co/9n8O4iBm2U.

NEARLY 500 DRONES, AND A FIRST AT SEA

Zelensky said on 12 September that Russia launched nearly 500 strike drones across Ukraine overnight. Ukrainian officials said drone strikes on two Ukrainian steel plants killed two people and injured six. Those counts come from Zelensky and from Ukrainian officials as relayed in today's packet, which records no independent verification of them. A Russian missile also destroyed part of an apartment building in Odesa, continuing the strikes on Odesa residential buildings this brief led with yesterday.

Ukraine's Navy said its Sargan-3000 unmanned surface vessel destroyed a Russian naval drone in the Black Sea, calling it "the first-ever battle between unmanned naval boats". The claim comes from one belligerent's navy, and today's packet states that the report could not be independently verified.

Moldovan authorities briefly closed national airspace and several border crossings after a drone was detected near the border — a fresh detection, after the incident in Moldovan airspace this brief carried earlier in the week.

Bloomberg reported that Russia struck energy facilities and other sites across southern Ukraine while Ukrainian forces targeted an oil-refining hub deep inside Russia, a further exchange in the mutual long-range campaign against energy infrastructure this brief has been tracking. That item rests on a single outlet, and today's packet records that the article could not be retrieved in full.

Sources: Kyiv Independent, India Today, BBC, Bloomberg.

KYIV DRAWS UP FUEL-SHORTAGE PLANS

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city is "working through various plans" for possible fuel shortages, adding that "we must be prepared for different scenarios, including a bad one." He said the city does not have the resources to build shelters at every filling station, and does not have enough air-defence weapons to intercept incoming drones and missiles.

The planning follows the campaign against Kyiv's gas stations that this brief has covered through the week, including the 11 September attack that killed two people and injured twelve, among them a child. The contingency planning itself is reported primarily by the Kyiv Independent and is thin for that reason.

Sources: Kyiv Independent, Al Jazeera.

TODAY'S UNDERREPORTED STORIES

One item in today's packet is carried by a single citable outlet with a direct stake in the subject, and is set out here as that and nothing more. RT, Russian state media, reports that Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau has opened an investigation into Budanov, Zelensky's chief of staff and the former head of military intelligence. No other report-role outlet in today's packet carries the report, and the packet records it as largely absent from mainstream Western outlets at the time of writing.

The specifics attached to that report — a sum of money, and an assertion about recordings — are grave allegations against a named individual, resting on one interested source with no corroboration from any party without a stake in it. They are not repeated here. What is reportable is that the claim has been made, and by whom.

Sources: RT (Russian state media).

Hurtigruten: The Original Norwegian Coastal Voyage

Hurtigruten is one of the world's most distinctive cruise operators. Unlike traditional cruise lines that focus primarily on entertainment and resort-style experiences, Hurtigruten grew out of Norway's coastal transportation network and remains deeply connected to the country's maritime culture. Today it offers both its historic coastal voyages and premium "Signature" cruises along Norway's coast and into the Arctic.

A Brief History

Hurtigruten, meaning "The Fast Route," was founded in 1893 by Captain Richard With. At the time, travel and communication between northern and southern Norway were difficult and often dangerous. The Norwegian government sought a reliable coastal service, and Richard With accepted the challenge. His vessel, DS Vesteraalen, completed the first voyage in July 1893.

Key milestones include:

1893: First sailing between Trondheim and Hammerfest.
1898: Route extended south to Bergen.
1908: Kirkenes became the northern terminus.
1936: Daily departures began.
Post-WWII: Fleet rebuilt after major wartime losses.
Modern era: Transition from primarily transport vessels to a blend of transportation, tourism, and expedition cruising.

Today, Hurtigruten remains famous for its Bergen-to-Kirkenes route, often called "The World's Most Beautiful Voyage."

Fleet
Original Coastal Express Fleet

These ships operate the classic Bergen-Kirkenes service:

MS Kong Harald
MS Nordkapp
MS Nordlys
MS Nordnorge
MS Polarlys
MS Richard With
MS Vesterålen

Most carry approximately 500 to 620 guests.

Signature Fleet

Premium, all-inclusive vessels:

MS Trollfjord
MS Midnatsol (joined Signature fleet after refurbishment in 2026)
MS Finnmarken (formerly MS Otto Sverdrup)

These ships focus on slower-paced coastal exploration, longer port visits, and enhanced onboard experiences.

Destinations

Hurtigruten's primary focus is Norway's coastline, but its itineraries also visit:

Norway
Bergen
Ålesund
Trondheim
Bodø
Lofoten Islands
Tromsø
Honningsvåg (gateway to North Cape)
Kirkenes
Geirangerfjord (seasonally)
Hjørundfjord
Senja
Vesterålen islands
Arctic Destinations
Svalbard/Longyearbyen
Barents Sea
North Cape region
Cruise Philosophy

Hurtigruten differs markedly from mainstream cruise lines such as Royal Caribbean, Norwegian, or Carnival.

Smaller Ships

Most vessels carry:

490 to 620 guests on Coastal Express ships
500 to 570 guests on Signature ships

This allows access to smaller fjords, remote villages, and narrow waterways that larger ships cannot enter.

Guest-to-Crew Ratio

The ratio generally falls around:

7:1 to 8:1 on most ships

For example, MS Trollfjord carries roughly 638 to 822 passengers with about 75 crew members.

The result is a more intimate, expedition-style atmosphere.

Ship Layout and Design Philosophy
Scandinavian Design

Hurtigruten ships emphasize:

Natural woods
Stone finishes
Large observation windows
Comfortable lounges
Functional elegance rather than flashy décor

The design aims to keep passengers visually connected to the landscape.

Public Areas

Most ships include:

Panoramic observation lounges
Large outdoor viewing decks
Lecture halls
Cafés and bars
Libraries
Fitness rooms
Saunas
Outdoor hot tubs on many vessels

Unlike mega-ships, there are no casinos, water parks, Broadway theaters, or shopping malls.

Staterooms and Suites

Accommodation generally falls into four categories:

Inside Cabins
Comfortable, compact
Private bathroom
Ideal for value-focused travelers
Outside Cabins
Picture windows or portholes
Views of coastal scenery
Superior Cabins
Larger floorplans
Better locations
Suites
Sitting areas
Enhanced amenities
Some with balconies on Signature ships
Priority services and premium touches
Dining

Hurtigruten pioneered its "Norway's Coastal Kitchen" concept.

Menus feature:

Arctic char
King crab
Norwegian salmon
Reindeer
Local cheeses
Regional produce sourced from coastal suppliers

Signature voyages include upgraded culinary offerings, specialty dining, and all-inclusive beverage programs.

Educational and Enrichment Experiences

One of Hurtigruten's greatest strengths is its educational focus.

Expedition Team

Signature sailings feature larger onboard expedition teams that provide:

Destination lectures
Arctic wildlife talks
Norwegian history presentations
Cultural demonstrations
Photography workshops
Storytelling sessions
Learning Opportunities

Guests often attend talks on:

Viking history
Coastal ecology
Sami culture
Arctic exploration
Geology and fjords
Northern Lights science
Shore Excursions

Popular excursions include:

North Cape visits
Dog sledding
Snowmobiling
King crab safaris
Lofoten kayaking
Guided fjord hikes
E-bike tours
Sami cultural experiences
Birdwatching
Wildlife safaris
Five Most Popular Sailings
1. Coastal Express Roundtrip

Bergen → Kirkenes → Bergen

12 days
34 ports
The classic voyage

Most iconic Hurtigruten itinerary.

2. Coastal Express Northbound

Bergen → Kirkenes

7 days
Considered the most scenic direction.
3. The North Cape Line

Oslo → North Cape → Oslo

Winter-focused
Northern Lights emphasis
Longer port stays
4. The Svalbard Line

Bergen → Longyearbyen → Bergen

Arctic-focused summer voyage
Midnight Sun
Wildlife viewing
Historic recreation of early Arctic routes
5. Astronomy Cruise

Special North Cape Line departures hosted by astronomer Tom Kerss featuring dedicated skywatching and aurora programs.

Embarkation Points

Main departure ports include:

Coastal Express
Bergen
Kirkenes
North Cape Line
Oslo
Hamburg (certain departures)
Svalbard Line
Bergen
Longyearbyen, Svalbard
Upcoming Spring Sailings

For spring seasons, Hurtigruten highlights:

Coastal Express
Regular Bergen-Kirkenes departures throughout spring.
Waterfalls are at peak flow from snowmelt.
Longer daylight hours.
Snow-capped mountains contrast with green valleys.
North Cape Line
Spring departures feature late-season Northern Lights opportunities in March and growing daylight through April and May.
Svalbard Line
Typically begins seasonal operations in late spring and continues through summer, linking Bergen with Longyearbyen during the Midnight Sun season.
New Nordic Programs

Recent Hurtigruten offerings include:

Arctic Norway Frontier Tour
Discover Norway with Summer Arctic Cabin Adventure
Best of Norway
Grand Nordic Adventure

Several begin from May and combine rail journeys, coastal sailings, fjords, and Arctic experiences.

Who Is Hurtigruten Best For?

Hurtigruten is ideal for travelers who want:

✅ Norwegian culture rather than cruise-ship entertainment
 ✅ Scenic fjords and small ports
 ✅ Northern Lights and Arctic landscapes
 ✅ Lectures and educational programming
 ✅ Excellent regional cuisine
 ✅ Smaller ships with fewer than 600 guests

It is less ideal for travelers seeking mega-ship attractions such as casinos, Broadway shows, water parks, or nonstop nightlife. Hurtigruten's focus is firmly on the destination rather than the ship itself.

SAME ADULT HEROINE IN EVERY SHOT:
A very beautiful young adult Korean woman, age 25–28, with luminous fair warm-toned skin and realistic pores, expressive dark-brown eyes, softly sculpted youthful cheeks, naturally beautiful full rose-pink lips with a subtle satin finish, natural understated Korean makeup, and a warm spontaneous smile. Preserve her facial geometry, body proportions and identity across every cut, without idealized plastic smoothing. Thin dark-metal oval prescription glasses with clear lenses, eyes always readable. Long, naturally dark-brown to soft-black hair, smooth and healthy with subtle natural movement; no blonde hair, no bangs.

One consistent modern Korean Gen Z outfit: an elegant loose ivory ankle-length A-line dress with full-length sleeves and a high neckline, subtle delicate embroidery, paired with a lightweight oversized beige cardigan jacket, clean cream sneakers, and a small structured taupe crossbody bag. Fabric remains naturally flowing, fully opaque and modest during movement. Glasses, hairstyle, outfit and bag remain identical throughout. Contemporary Korean styling, youthful, effortlessly elegant and understated. No spaghetti straps, revealing neckline, exposed midriff, or body-hugging styling. There is no supplied reference image: establish this original Korean heroine from these text details and maintain her exact identity. Never morph into another woman, change her ethnicity, facial features, hairstyle, or body proportions.

MINIDV STYLE LOCK:
Feels like a cherished home-video cassette recorded around 2003, not polished cinema pretending to be vintage. Gentle optical softness, low contrast, softly washed highlights, warm natural skin, fine luma noise, mild color bleed, subtle consumer-camera edge enhancement, restrained DV compression texture, slightly faded blues and greens, soft halation, occasional exposure pumping when moving between shade and sunlight.

Real handheld wide-angle proximity, uncentered composition, brief autofocus searching that settles on her face. Noticeable motion smear on fast pans and night lights, but keep expressions legible. No heavy glitch overlays, fake VHS tracking bars, film burns between scenes, timestamps, captions, subtitles, logos, or excessive chromatic aberration. Noon feels airy, sunset feels honey-gold, night feels softly smeared and imperfect. Do not use green-noir grading or glossy blockbuster teal-orange.

POV AND EDIT RULES:
The camera operator is her adult boyfriend, mostly unseen, occasionally one anatomically correct forearm or hand enters. She repeatedly checks where he is, leans toward him, looks back, shares a discovery, and smiles directly into the lens. Small natural gestures, no fashion posing, no slow-motion beauty commercial. Hold each simple action long enough to read. Hard cuts between locations, no morphing transitions.

Geography evokes a remembered Kansai day through Uji and Nara, with ordinary bookshops and shopping streets between famous places. Late spring or early summer green foliage; no contradictory autumn leaves, snow or cherry blossoms. Do not squeeze in extra landmarks or relocate Mount Fuji into Nara.

EXACT 30-SECOND EDIT:

00.00–04.00 — SUBURBAN PLATFORM, DANGER THEN RELIEF
Open with danger already readable: she has distractedly stepped too near the platform edge while peering down the line, one hand shading her eyes. She remains on the platform, never on the rails. An approaching maroon-and-cream commuter train is already visible behind her and rapidly grows larger.

From first-person POV, one boyfriend hand reaches to her upper arm; upon contact, the arm immediately retracts in ONE continuous movement, pulling her backward toward the lens and behind the tactile safety strip. She visibly moves back one or two quick steps; camera operator steps back naturally with her. Only once she is clear does the train rush past behind her.

Its wind flutters her overshirt and dress hem, never lifts or removes her hijab or exposes her body. Her eyes widen behind glasses, lips part with a brief startled gasp, then relief begins in her expression. No contact with the train, injuries, lingering on the edge, or repeated pulling motion. Believable distances and train direction; staged fictional action with a clearly successful rescue. Keep one continuous shot for this opening.

04.00–06.00 — SUNNY GRASS
Abrupt warm hard cut: first-person handholding as she guides the viewer along a grassy path. She turns toward the camera with a relieved bright laugh. Sunlight catches her ivory sleeves and navy floral hijab pin; green grass drifts softly behind. One hand linked naturally with the operator, no duplicate fingers.

06.00–07.50 — OLD BOOKSHOP
Shoot through a gap between shelves of well-used Japanese books. She playfully bends into the gap from the far side, notices the lens, gives a small conspiratorial smile. Dusty window light, crowded wooden shelves, autofocus briefly catches book spines before her eyes. Avoid legible invented titles.

07.50–09.00 — QUIET STREET CROSSING
Low, casual waist-to-shoe framing of her walking across an ordinary Japanese zebra crossing on a pedestrian signal. Ivory dress hem sways over trainers. Tilt just enough to glimpse her looking back. No fetishized body framing; modest everyday clothing detail and footsteps are the focus.

09.00–10.50 — NARROW LANE
She walks ahead between traditional wooden storefronts, potted plants and hanging fabric curtains. Her eyes glance sideways first, then she turns her face back to find the camera, smiling softly. Overhead cables and bicycles at the side establish lived-in Japan; no staged crowd.

10.50–12.50 — UJI RIVERSIDE, ADDED RESEARCHED SCENE
At the scenic Uji River in Kyoto Prefecture, film her by a pedestrian riverbank with the historic bridge in the background. Begin with sunlight moving on water, tilt casually to her leaning lightly on the safe railing. A breeze moves her cuff; she points out the view, then looks at the operator rather than posing for the landscape. Keep her face central to the memory, river sound underneath.

12.50–14.00 — UJI MATCHA, ADDED RESEARCHED SCENE
Close handheld view of her holding a simple matcha soft-serve outside a small tea shop. She takes a tiny taste, raises her eyebrows appreciatively, then offers the cone toward the lens with a playful smile. Rich natural tea-green against ivory fabric; mild sunlight overexposure, soft storefront background. No visible brand text.

14.00–15.50 — SMALL RAMEN SHOP
Close-up of steaming vegetarian mushroom-and-vegetable ramen on a wooden counter or small table, then a quick natural focus pull to her sitting opposite, smiling through wisps of steam. Cozy lamps, spoon and bowl sounds, genuine restaurant ambience. No pork slices or alcohol props. Camera remains handheld, not a glossy food advertisement.

15.50–17.00 — MANGA SHOP
She draws one manga volume from a shelf, opens it and lowers her eyes with a curious smile. Brief close shot of hands and page texture; no readable dialogue or famous copyrighted character emphasis. Maintain same glasses and floral pin.

17.00–18.50 — NARA PARK DEER
Boyfriend POV offers one designated deer cracker, held flat and released gently to a deer in Nara Park. The woman is softly out of focus a few steps behind on green grass, laughing at the deer's polite approach. No grabbing antlers, hugging or chasing wildlife. Mild camera wobble as the deer approaches.

18.50–20.00 — QUIET READING
Sitting on a park bench, she flips a manga page. Close details of her hands, gold botanical embroidery and lace cuff, then tilt to her peaceful face behind her glasses. Rustle of paper, leaves and distant birds. Natural, modest, unposed.

20.00–22.50 — UKIMIDO PAVILION, ADDED RESEARCHED SCENE
Nara Park's hexagonal wooden Ukimido pavilion with its cypress-bark roof on Sagiike Pond, reached by a wooden bridge. From the public bridge, she pauses safely by the railing and turns back toward the camera; warm light and green trees reflect in still water. Start wide enough to read the actual pavilion silhouette, then walk a little closer as she extends her hand toward the viewer. Quiet water, wooden footfalls, no temple ritual invented. Intimate location memory rather than a drone tourism shot.

22.50–24.50 — GOLDEN-HOUR MEADOW
In Nara's grassy park with deer grazing at a respectful distance, honey-gold backlight edges her hijab and sleeves. She turns gently toward the camera, dress fabric swaying with the evening breeze. A small genuine smile, peaceful eye contact, slight exposure bloom. No spinning near deer, no flying fabric revealing skin.

24.50–27.00 — LIVELY NIGHT SHOPPING STREET
Blue-hour-to-night hard cut. Warm shop lanterns, illuminated signs and pedestrians in a Kansai shopping street. She suddenly jogs lightly several steps ahead, then looks back laughing, waiting for the operator. He follows; handheld camera movement leaves convincing soft DV light streaks. No vehicles in her running path; stay in a pedestrian area. Preserve facial readability between movement smears.

27.00–28.00 — TACTILE MEMORY INSERT
One brief close handheld detail of her hand adjusting her embroidered cuff beside her taupe bag, ivory skirt hanging naturally; warm shop light blooms softly off the stitching. A casual recorded detail, not an erotic crop.
28.00–30.00 — CAMCORDER MEMORY ENDING
A second small silver early-2000s consumer camcorder is held into the foreground by the operator's free hand, its side LCD flipped outward. Current POV remains on the original recording camera; make this a clearly separate physical device, not an impossible view of itself.

The second camcorder points toward the woman; its LCD shows the same woman in the same pose at the same moment, synchronized without a duplicate person standing nearby. She notices that he is still filming, briefly gives a playful tiny pout with her naturally rose-toned lips, then breaks into a real warm laugh looking directly at him. Frame drifts toward a bright shop lamp and highlights bloom to soft white over the final fraction of a second. End on warmth, not alarm.

Real synchronized location sound ONLY, no background music, no soundtrack, no narration, no scripted dialogue.
