I’m glad Apple finally solved the foldable problem. Now they can focus on technology where you don’t have to fold anything at all:

AirPods with IR. Smart glasses. AR glasses. Vision Pro.

I don’t see these as separate pieces of tech. I see them as part of the Apple halo effect, different devices working together as pieces of a much larger wearable computing ecosystem, and potentially an entirely new economy around it.

Apple has spent years solving difficult problems around displays, batteries, modems, materials, miniaturization and thermal management. “Vapor chamber” just sounds cool, like Apple calling a CD/DVD player a SuperDrive back in the day.

A lot of that engineering matters far beyond a folding phone.

I agree with the rumors and think we’ll see a range of XR tech, from increasingly intelligent AirPods and lightweight smart glasses to more capable AR glasses, with Vision Pro sitting at the high end.

And I still wholeheartedly believe Vision Pro has enormous potential.

The iPhone App Store is mature, crowded and facing increasing pressure around commissions and distribution from Epic, regulators and developers themselves.

Apple needs new platforms where developers can create entirely new categories of apps, services and content.

XR can offer Apple all of that while building on platforms it already has in place.
It also opens up entirely new revenue opportunities through entertainment. Concerts, movies and, most of all, sports.

There’s a reason people pay big bucks to sit behind home plate, rub shoulders court side, watch from the 50 yard line or fight for the best spot at the race track.

Perspective has value.

If Vision Pro can deliver that feeling of being there for every game, race or event, people will pay for it. Subscriptions, season packages, premium viewpoints, pay per view, team packages and things we probably haven’t thought of yet.

And I don’t think for a second that immersive entertainment replaces actually going to these events. I just feel it becomes another viable option.

When I start adding up the cost of tickets, gas, parking, food and everything else, suddenly the price of a wearable itself becomes a little easier to justify. At least to me.

The 2028 LA Olympics could be an incredible opportunity for Apple to prove what immersive sports can look like across dozens of events in one place.
But there’s another major hurdle if any of this is going to become mainstream: privacy.

Apple has spent years building a reputation around protecting user data, and I think that could become one of its biggest advantages as wearables move into public spaces.

The more Apple can rely on IR depth sensing, on-device processing and other sensor technologies without making everything dependent on traditional cameras, the easier it becomes for people to feel comfortable around these devices. That work might eventually pay dividends in areas like personal robotics too.

For wearables to become mainstream, it isn’t enough for the person wearing them to trust the technology. Everyone around them has to trust it too.
I really love my Oakley smart glasses, but I don’t always feel comfortable wearing them in public because I’m aware of how other people might perceive them.
If Apple can make privacy part of the hardware architecture, not just part of the marketing, that could become one of the most important things it brings to XR.

And this is where I think things start getting really interesting.

XR is getting close to the point where several technologies are converging at once:
Better sensors. More efficient modems. Smaller displays and optics. Apple silicon. Strong privacy protections. Great eye and hand tracking.

Then add the piece that could tie all of it together: a genuinely useful AI agent.

Take away the mouse, keyboard and trackpad and you’re left with your hands, your eyes and your voice.
Apple already has the eye tracking. Vision Pro’s implementation is by far the best I’ve personally experienced.

Now give me voice support and an AI that actually understands what I’m looking at, what I’m doing and what I want.

That’s when this stops feeling like apps running on a headset and starts feeling like a new computing platform.

That’s the part is personal for me.

@RevirStudios is focused on XR and wearable tools that can help people with mobility challenges gain more independence and interact with the world in new ways.
So I can look at Vision Pro through entertainment, sports, apps, business, or the consumer market.
But the question I care about most is simpler:
What can this do for someone who has fewer physical options available to them?

That’s why I keep paying attention to where Apple takes this.

I’m glad they figured out how to fold the screen.
Now I want to see them spend the next decade making the screen disappear.

Thank you for coming to my early morning, coffee-fueled, non-TED talk.  😀

text:
Dex Hunter-Torricke, ex-Google DeepMind comms chief, on why the entire AI safety debate is a distraction from what's actually coming:

Dex spent two decades inside the machine, running communications for Elon Musk at SpaceX, writing Mark Zuckerberg's speeches at Facebook, and leading Global Communications and Marketing at Google DeepMind from 2023 to 2025.

He left in late 2025 and founded the Center for Tomorrow in February 2026. This is what he says now:

"We talk about AI governance. Yeah. And there's a whole bunch of stuff which is about how you manage the AI systems themselves. That's like 1% of the problem."

One percent. That's the entire debate you've been reading about for three years.

What worries him is the slope the technology is on:

"...how quickly it is gathering steam, how much more advanced it's getting, how much more advanced it will be in the next decade. That is something which is going to be wildly more devastating than any of the consequences of the mismanaged technologies of the last 15 years."

His benchmark is the wreckage of the last 15 years, social media and platform power included, and he's saying that was the warm-up:

"And the consequences will crash land on societies all over the world. We are not prepared for these things at all economically, society, geopolitically, environmentally. And that's the agenda that I'm really focused on. The tech industry has massively distorted the agenda for how to manage these things."

So what's the other 99%?

First, work. The job losses worry him less than the silence where the solution should be:

"15 years from now, probably less than 15 years when a lot of people have lost their jobs to AI and we have no economic solutions. We have no idea how to give people a good quality of life. That is a much much bigger problem than some of the technical issues we're facing in those systems."

We have no idea. From the man who wrote the speeches.

Second, the physical bill. AI runs on power, water, land and minerals, and it's coming for ecosystems that are already spent:

"...destabilize already reeling ecosystems which we know are hanging by a thread and which will impact the lives of millions if not billions of people."

His number:

"Between 2018 and 2023 the world consumed almost as much resources as one-third of the 20th century and it's accelerating all the time."

Five years, against roughly thirty-three. Accelerating.

Third, and this is the part that makes it hard to stop. Dex describes the pitch he watched get made to governments with nothing left to offer voters:

"Big tech companies, they go to governments who are desperate for economic growth now, right. A lot of the advanced economies in the global north, they've got plateauing growth. They've got declining living standards. They go to them and say, 'Build this wonder technology. Build this infrastructure. We will give you back the keys to a good future.'"

His verdict is four words:

"And of course, that's not happening."

"This is something which on the present path promises to enrich a tiny sliver of societies, mostly in the United States, mostly in China."

"I think the world we're going to end up in, you know, in the next, you know, 10, 15 years is going to be much more unstable than today with rapidly declining living standards for hundreds of millions."

text:
God Bless our Military and Patriotic and Loving  Americans! 

I  BET YOU DIDN'Y KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED.
A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants
who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the
children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.
There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who
would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to
bundle them into carriers and strollers.
Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they
needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran
back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well,
here we are, on our own."
About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.
Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up
toddlers.
The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of
the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .
Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped
in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the
cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the
Old West.
Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from
wandering off. Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter
around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until
the parents could be notified and come get their children.
The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on
any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men
there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.
The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted;
could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories
from the Pentagon.
It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life,
liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. It's the military who salutes the
flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.
If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for
the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have
served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those 
who have given the ultimate sacrifice!                                                                                                                                                               
  God Bless The USA!
Never forget!!!

Number 9: Keep in mind the following tools.

1: Rosemary oil + EVOO or apricot oil or ricebran oil.

Rosemary oil is rich in carnosic acid, ursolic acid and rosmarinic acid that enhance scalp blood flow, upregulate VEGF and IGF-1, promoting anagen.

It’s also an alternative to 2% minoxidil for people who do not react well to it or don’t want to try it.

In a study, rosemary oil led to a 22% hair count increase and topical 2% minoxidil to 19%.

(Yes, rosemary oil, inhibits 5-AR topically).

Rosmarinic acid also has broader anti-inflammatory properties and reduces IL-6/TNF-α and carnosic acid has great antioxidant properties.

Crucial note: Dilute the rosemary oil in a carrier oil such as EVOO (extra virgin olive oil), apricot oil or ricebran oil.

EVOO is rich in tocopherols and oleic acid.

Vitamin E neutralizes reactive oxygen species (ROS), protecting dermal papilla cells (DPCs) and hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs) from oxidative stress and the oleic acid hydrates the scalp.

Apricot oil is rich in vitamins A, C, E, K and minerals (magnesium, manganese, phosphorus, potassium).

Vitamins A/C/E and minerals support keratin synthesis and HFSC health, enhancing hair elasticity and reducing breakage.

Vitamin E and magnesium support VEGF and FGF-7 (in inflamed scalps).

Rice bran oil contains oleic/linoleic acids, vitamins E/K and antioxidants such as γ-oryzanol.

2: Aspirin, taurine and caffeine (NOT for dry scalps).

In this one, aspirin is used since it inhibits COX-1/COX-2 enzymes, reducing PGD2 and it may improve scalp blood flow.

Taurine is used since it protects hair follicles from TGF-β1-induced fibrosis that is another key AGA driver and it may enhance VEGF.

Caffeine is used because it stimulates hair follicle growth by inhibiting phosphodiesterase (PDE), increasing cAMP levels, which promotes anagen phase and counters DHT-induced follicle miniaturization.

3: Nettler root and taurine (safer for people who have AGA and dry scalps) with EVOO and apricot oil as carrier oils.

Nettle inhibits 5-LOX, reducing inflammatory prostaglandins but also DHT through 5-AR inhibition (nettle extract can be used in the first serum 1 if your scalp is quite oily as well).

Taurine as it was just stated, protects hair follicles from TGF-β1-induced fibrosis that is another key AGA driver and it may enhance VEGF.

4: Organic castor oil, wheat germ oil, Japanese mint oil and jojoba oil (mainly for TE, AA and AE (could be used for AGA as well)).

Castor oil is rich in ricinoleic acid that enhances scalp blood flow, has antimicrobial properties and can help combat fungal infections.

Wheat germ oils has vitamin E and linoleic acid that mainly help with hydration.

Japanese mint oil increases scalp blood flow and has anti-inflammatory properties overall.

5: EVOO, horsetail extract, nettle root extract and tea tree oil OR grapefruit seed extract (can be used for most types of hair loss when paired with danrduff but not for people who have dry scalps).

Once again, EVOO is rich in oleic acid and tocopherols so it hydrates the scalp, neutralizes reactive oxygen species (ROS) and protects dermal papilla cells (DPCs) and hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs) from oxidative stress.

Horsetail extract contains a lot of silica (7–10%), flavonoids and antioxidants crucial for collagen and keratin synthesis (in vitro, silica enhances DPC proliferation).

Tea tree oil contains terpinen-4-ol that provides antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects, reducing scalp conditions like dandruff or folliculitis that can exacerbate hair loss.

But in case tea tree oil is too strong for your scalp, you can consider replacing it with grapefruit seed extract that contains flavonoids such as naringin, polyphenols and citric acid, with antimicrobial, antifungal, and antioxidant properties that in vitro studies have shown that they inhibit fungi such as Malassezia.

6: Onion juice for individuals with AA and dandruff.

*Start by juicing just 1 onion once a week (leave it for just 3 minutes (yes 3, not 30) the first time (you can do up to 10 minutes after assessing tolerance) and obviously rinse it afterwards).

7: Niacinamide and taurine (you can use caffeine as well).

Niacinamide offers general antioxidant protection/reduces oxidative stress in dermal papilla cells downregulates DKK-1 and improves circulation.

8: Pumpkin seed oil, rosemary oil, EVOO and apricot oil.

This is the perfect option for people with AGA and very oily hair.

Pumpkin seed oil is even more effective than rosemary oil against minoxidil.

Rosemary oil is almost as effective as 2% minoxidil and pumpkin seed oil is almost as effective as 5% minoxidil (in a randomized control trial).

Pumpkin seed oil contains phytosterols such as beta-sitosterol and fatty acids such as linoleic and oleic.

It basically works by topical inhibition of 5-alpha-reductase.

Note: Three more topicals that might sound weird but can help are:

Ashwagandha

Green tea extract

Topical thyroid hormones

text:
The Last Ghosts

When I was a young man growing up in a rural outport community, the old folks used to tell us ghost stories. Many came from the years before electrical power reached the place, when night settled over the peninsula and there was little anyone could do to hold it back.

We had one road. It ran through the community and ended near the tip of the peninsula. Along the way, several brooks crossed beneath it, carrying water down toward the sea.

I heard many stories about things people had encountered on that road. But what stayed with me was the advice that accompanied them.

If a spirit followed you, run for a brook crossing.

The clergy gave us an explanation: where the brook crossed the road, it formed a cross. Reach that place and you would be under the protection of Christ.

As a young man, I accepted that. Later, I began to wonder whether the water itself mattered.

Perhaps the cross was simply the explanation people gave to something they believed they had observed.

That thought became the beginning of my theory.

I began to imagine the brooks as paths, something like the invisible routes people call ley lines. In my mind, those paths followed the water through the land and eventually out to sea.

What if the dead could feel them?

What if, after the body failed, something of us remained—confused, unmoored, still drawn to familiar places? Perhaps most souls eventually found a current that carried them home, back into the earth and the waters from which life came.

Others might linger.

A violent death. An injustice. A grief too heavy to leave behind. Perhaps these could bind a person to a house or a stretch of road long after everyone who remembered them had gone.

That was how I began to understand the old stories: some of the dead were still finding their way.

Then we brought in electricity.

We strung wires along the roads, carried them across the brooks, and pulled them through the walls of our houses. We laid cables beneath the sea. Within a few generations, we had surrounded ourselves with a vast, interconnected system of currents.

We switched on the lights.

And, in the story I cannot quite put out of my mind, the ghosts began to disappear.

You might say we had ghostbusted the world.

It sounds almost funny, until you consider where they might have gone.

Suppose whatever survives us can be drawn toward a current. Suppose the faint pathways I imagined in the natural world once offered it a way home.

What would happen when something far more powerful came within reach?

A person dies in a bedroom. Their family is gathered close. Someone leaves a lamp burning beside the bed.

And whatever rises from that body never reaches the door.

It is caught before it understands that it has died.

Pulled into the wiring. Carried beyond the house. Swept into a system with no shore, no resting place, and no destination intended for anything that has ever been human.

The lights stay on. The family grieves. No one sees anything unusual.

That is the possibility that frightens me: an artificial afterlife, built into the ordinary world.

An endless harvesting, with no one assigned to collect the harvest and no one aware that it is happening.

I am not suggesting anyone intended it. An accident would be terrible enough. We could have built the whole thing in perfect innocence, celebrating every new connection, bringing light to another isolated house.

Thomas Edison provides a strange historical footnote. In 1920, he told interviewers that he was working on an apparatus intended to investigate whether the dead could communicate. He did not promise success. His proposal depended on the possibility that something of human personality survived and could influence a sufficiently sensitive instrument. According to the Thomas A. Edison Papers at Rutgers, no verifiable evidence of his work on such a device has ever been found. Source: Thomas A. Edison Papers

That proves nothing about my theory. But there is something unsettling about a man who helped electrify the world also wondering whether a machine could detect what remained of us after death.

He imagined an instrument through which the dead might make themselves known.

I imagine a system in which they could disappear without ever being heard.

Perhaps there would be no awareness at all. Perhaps everything that made you yourself would simply come apart.

Or perhaps you would remain.

You might remember your name. Your children. The room where you died. You might spend whatever passes for time trying to return to it, carried through a thousand houses without ever being able to enter one.

And all the while, the living would be congratulating themselves on having outgrown ghost stories.

I think about those brooks now. The little crossings on our single road. The water moving steadily toward the sea.

The old folks told us where to run.

If my theory were true, there might be nowhere close enough anymore.

We used to be afraid that the dead could find their way back to us.

Now I wonder whether a haunting would be a mercy: one person still free enough to stand in a doorway, to be recognized, to let someone know they had survived.

We don’t have ghosts anymore.

I used to find that comforting.

Now, when I remember the old stories, I find myself hoping someone still sees one.

Throughout his Conquest of Europe William left a wake of not only destruction but mistresses, in turn also establishing various permanent settlements & such too...some of which offspring were eventually "wisked" away & taken in by some of the more prominent clans who were able to offer protections & taken into hiding as their own kinfolk.

For some time we remained largely independent settlements mingling & breeding among the other local clans & were what are known as Border Reivers...meaning we belonged to a collection of largely Norse mixed with Gael Clans that would regularly pillage both England, Scotland & Eire (Pirate's of the land essentially).

We'd later came to loyally serve the Scottish throne up until it's usurpation by our cousins (now known as the Windsor's...the current "Royal" Family) where we lived humbly as Septs to the McNaughton's who'd, working with other clans & our brothers & sisters over in Eire, kept our lineage safe & secret for generations upon generations... 
Until more recent times.

Upon the betrayal of young Queen Mary & her father James we were made to change our names and flee Scotland together with what remaining nobility who were not slain or ended up siding with the enemy in this ongoing & utterly TREACHEROUS family feud and we were taken in as prominent members of Ulster in Eire/"Ireland" (hence where the term "Ulster Scots" came from) and then made to flee or die again sometime later during the famine caused by the British Conquest of Eire where we came to The America's having mingled back in with the common folk all coming to the New World en-masse.

My grandfather Wilf (Wilfred) was then born in Salt Lake City Utah where we'd originally settled upon coming to The America's but then due to the never-ending hardships & being nothing short of hunted down & f***ed with at every turn even all the way across the Atlantic my grandfather Wilf (Wilfred) was sent from Salt Lake City in Utah all the way here to Canada, then one of the most secluded & remote places inhabited places left on this world, to be raised by a relatively established family in the extremely remote & newly established Capital of British Columbia, Victoria.

Then upon my Grandfather coming of age & moving out on his own and with the history all behind us (err.., thought to had been) he'd changed his name back from "Woolridge" to the surname we'd taken upon ourselves after coming to serve the Scottish Throne several hundred years ago...which was only around 6-8 lifetimes ago...which is really not all that long at all when one actually thinks about it.

We have direct historical relations & ties to not just the current British "Royal family" (our distant cousins) though William The Conqueror & others but have had close ties to Norway, The Scottish Throne (particularly under James & young Queen Mary, England, France & Charlamagne among other places, families & figures I need not get into here & now. 

Life is strange, no?

And in case anyone was ever wondering if there are any  descendants left remaining of the original throne of England before it's having been conquered & the current "Royal" family line established there...

Yes there are...
They are of Welsh background & currently live in Australia...

And have been known to rather adamantly state when asked about the subject that they want ABSOLUTELY NOTHING to do with any of it & to just leave them alone. 

Which is respectable in their own way too.

text:
The architecture in this graphic is not a security doctrine. It is a demand that the region ratify the Islamic Republic as the unaccountable hub of West Asia while the costs of its behavior are reclassified as “coercion” by everyone else.

Start with the first pillar: peaceful coexistence and freedom of navigation. Iran spent years treating the Strait of #Hormuz and the Red Sea as instruments of leverage, not as public goods. A state that uses maritime chokepoints as bargaining chips cannot then claim that “freedom of #navigation” is its principle. That is not coexistence. It is conditional access.
Sovereign equality and non-aggression collapse on contact with the record. Non-interference is incompatible with a three-decade project of arming, financing, and directing non-state actors across Lebanon, Iraq, Syria, and Yemen. Reciprocal security guarantees require a counterpart that can be verified. Proxy networks exist precisely to deny attribution and evade that verification. You cannot sell “binding non-aggression” while retaining the option of deniable force.
International rule of law is the most revealing line. “Reject coercive unilateral measures” and “multilateral oversight (IAEA, UN)” only work if the oversight is accepted when it is inconvenient. #IAEA reporting on undeclared nuclear activity, incomplete declarations, and restricted access is not a Western talking point. It is the multilateral record. Recasting every enforcement tool as illegitimate coercion is not legalism. It is an attempt to keep the benefits of NPT membership without the constraints.
Balanced security and shared development sounds like economics. In practice it is a bid to convert sanctions relief and energy integration into political immunity. Trade and consortiums can stabilize a status quo. They cannot substitute for a change in the behavior that produced the isolation: nuclear opacity, regional militarization through proxies, and a domestic order that treats dissent as a security threat.
China’s offer of mediation is realpolitik, not a moral reset. Beijing is a major buyer of Iranian oil, a sanctions-evasion partner, and a power with its own coercive toolkit. That does not make it a neutral architect of “inclusive multilateralism.” It makes it a stakeholder with an interest in a weakened U.S. position and a surviving Iranian system.
The closing slogan — “#security cannot be bought at the expense of others” — is inverted. The expense has already been paid by neighbors living under missile and militia threat, by shippers facing disruption, and by Iranians living under a security state that exports instability while demanding immunity at home.
A scientific security order starts from observable behavior, not from pillars drawn around a map of Iran. Credible commitments need verification, reciprocity that can be measured, and an end to dual-use ambiguity — nuclear, maritime, and proxy. Until those are on the table, this is not a foundation for peace. It is a brief for the same architecture that produced the current war.

text:
Reporter Ariela Karmel: If the makeup of B’Yachad’s slate reveals what kind of politicians the party believes Israelis want, the crowd Sunday offered an equally revealing picture of the voters it now appears to be seeking.

The event felt unmistakably liberal and Tel Avivian: young, secular and fervently opposed to the current government and its policies, though not necessarily comfortable with the political left as represented by Yair Golan’s Democrats. 

Sunday’s event suggested B’Yachad is no longer organizing itself around winning right-leaning voters back, but is embracing the constituency it actually has: liberal-Zionist, largely centrist Israelis animated by military and national service, competent government, a state commission of inquiry into October 7 and an end to sweeping Haredi draft exemptions.

It is not a small constituency. Whether it is a large enough one to fulfill Bennett’s ambitions is another matter.

Read more on The Times of Israel.

text:
The Glorious Mysteries of the Rosary: The Ascension: A Promise of Our Own Ascension

As the disciples stood gazing into the heavens, watching their Lord and Savior ascend to His Father, they were filled with awe and a profound sense of anticipation. The Ascension of Jesus Christ was not merely a departure but a promise—a promise that we, too, will one day ascend to be with Him in glory. This event, celebrated by the Church, is a beacon of hope and a testament to our ultimate destiny as believers. Today, we delve into the profound mystery of the Ascension and how it prefigures our own ascent into eternal life, drawing from the wisdom of St. Paul, the teachings of the Catechism, and the insights of the saints.

The Ascension of Jesus Christ marks the culmination of His earthly mission and the beginning of His reign at the right hand of the Father. It is a pivotal moment in salvation history, as described in the Acts of the Apostles: "As they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight" (Acts 1:9). This event is not just a historical occurrence; it is a theological reality that speaks to our own journey towards heaven.

St. Paul, in his letters, provides profound insights into the significance of the Ascension for our own salvation. In his letter to the Ephesians, he writes, "He who descended is he who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things" (Ephesians 4:10). St. Paul emphasizes that Christ's Ascension is not just a return to His divine state but a fulfillment of His mission to redeem humanity. By ascending, Christ opens the way for us to follow Him into the heavenly realm.

The Catechism of the Catholic Church further illuminates this truth, stating, "By his death and Resurrection, Jesus Christ has 'opened' heaven to us. The life of the blessed consists in the full and perfect possession of the fruits of the redemption accomplished by Christ" (CCC 1026). The Ascension, therefore, is a promise of our own ascension, a guarantee that we will share in the glory of Christ if we remain faithful to Him.

To deepen our understanding of this mystery, we turn to the wisdom of the saints. St. Augustine, in his reflections on the Ascension, beautifully articulates the hope it instills in us: "Our Lord Jesus Christ ascended into heaven, and there He sits at the right hand of the Father, and He will come again to judge the living and the dead. This is our faith, this is our hope." St. Augustine reminds us that the Ascension is not just an event of the past but a living hope that sustains us in our journey towards heaven.

St. Thomas Aquinas, a Doctor of the Church, also provides profound insights into the theological significance of the Ascension. In his Summa Theologica, he explains that the Ascension was necessary for the completion of our redemption: "It was fitting for Christ to ascend into heaven, first, because heaven was due to Him by reason of His divine nature; and secondly, because He ascended in order to send the Holy Ghost upon His disciples." Aquinas underscores that the Ascension is not just a departure but a necessary step in the unfolding of God's plan for our salvation.

The Ascension also has profound implications for our daily lives as Christians. In his encyclical "Spe Salvi," Pope Benedict XVI reflects on the hope that the Ascension instills in us: "The belief that at the end of life we will be taken up into a state of eternal life and happiness does not diminish but rather enhances our commitment to building a better world here and now." The promise of our own ascension calls us to live with greater purpose and dedication, knowing that our actions here on earth have eternal consequences.

This call to live with hope and purpose is echoed in the teachings of recent popes. In his apostolic exhortation "Evangelii Gaudium," Pope Francis emphasizes the transformative power of the Ascension: "The Gospel, radiant with the glory of Christ's cross, constantly invites us to rejoice. A joy ever new, a joy that is the same as the initial joy of those who encountered Jesus along the way." The Ascension reminds us that our ultimate joy is found in Christ and that we are called to share this joy with others.

In our contemporary world, the promise of the Ascension offers a countercultural message of hope and redemption. In a society often marked by despair and materialism, the Ascension calls us to look beyond the temporal and to fix our eyes on the eternal. It challenges us to live with a sense of purpose and to strive for holiness, knowing that our ultimate destiny is to be with Christ in heaven.

As we reflect on the Ascension and its promise for our own lives, we are reminded of the continuity of our faith from past to present. The teachings of St. Paul, the insights of the Catechism, and the wisdom of the saints all point to the same truth: that Christ's Ascension is a promise of our own ascension. This promise is not just a theological concept but a living reality that shapes our lives and our hope for the future.

In conclusion, the Ascension of Jesus Christ is a profound mystery that speaks to the heart of our faith. It is a promise that we, too, will one day ascend to be with Him in glory if we remain faithful. As we celebrate this feast, let us renew our commitment to living with hope and purpose, knowing that our ultimate destiny is to share in the joy of Christ's kingdom.

How can the promise of the Ascension inspire you to live with greater hope and purpose in your daily life? Let us ponder this question and allow the mystery of the Ascension to transform our hearts and minds, drawing us ever closer to the Lord who has gone before us to prepare a place for us in His Father's house.

The Glorious Mysteries of the Rosary celebrate the victory of Jesus and Mary over sin and death. These events inspire Catholics to live with faith and hope in daily life. The Resurrection brings assurance of eternal life to those who believe. The Ascension reminds believers of their heavenly destiny after earthly trials. The coming of the Holy Spirit empowers the Church with grace for mission. The Assumption honors Mary as mother and queen in heaven. The Coronation promises a share in heavenly glory for the faithful who persevere.
Catholics should contemplate the Ascension of Jesus into heaven. This mystery encourages detachment from worldly concerns that pull the soul downward. It directs hearts toward God and eternal rewards amid modern distractions. Believers gain strength to follow Christ upward through prayer and virtue.

text:
Third Edition of Gangtok Hill Trek Concludes, Tamjay–Phodong–Kabi Lungchok Trail Proposed for Eco-Tourism Development

The third edition of the Gangtok Hill Trek, jointly organised by the Sikkim Mountaineering Association (SMA) and the Mountaineering and Adventure Institute of Sikkim (MAIS), concluded successfully on September 12, with participation from students, government employees and local youth.

This year’s one-day trek explored the scenic Tamjay–Phodong–Kabi Lungchok route, showcasing its potential for adventure tourism and sustainable eco-tourism.

SMA President Kunzang Gyatso said the trail could be developed as a one-, two- or three-day trekking circuit, creating new livelihood and income opportunities for local communities while promoting responsible tourism.

He highlighted the need for better trail infrastructure, including small footbridges, regular maintenance, temporary monsoon shelters and designated camping sites. He also called for a simplified permit process to make the route more accessible to visitors.

SMA Secretary Prabin Khaling expressed gratitude to Namerakpam Jaswant, IFS (Wildlife and Forest Conservation), the DFO, Forest Department, Sikkim Police check-post personnel, the Indian Army’s 17 Mountain Division, Army personnel stationed in Tamjay, MAIS, SMA and the Tourism Department for their support.

According to the organisers, July to September offers an ideal trekking window, with lush greenery, alpine flora and scenic landscapes enhancing the experience.

SMA and MAIS said continued coordination among departments, security agencies and local stakeholders could help the Tamjay–Phodong–Kabi Lungchok trail emerge as one of Sikkim’s notable eco-tourism and adventure tourism destinations.

#GangtokHillTrek #Sikkim #EcoTourism #AdventureTourism #Trekking #SustainableTourism #Tamjay #Phodong #KabiLungchok #SMA #MAIS

text:
Exalting the Crucified Messiah
Monday, September 14, 2026
Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

Jesus said to Nicodemus: “No one has gone up to heaven except the one who has come down from heaven, the Son of Man. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.” John 3:13–15

Today, as we celebrate the great Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, we are invited to ponder Jesus’ conversation with Nicodemus, “a ruler of the Jews” (John 3:1). Nicodemus was one of the few Pharisees who believed in Jesus. In many Eastern Churches, he is honored as a saint.

Nicodemus approached Jesus early in His public ministry. By that time, Jesus had called some of His Apostles, performed His first sign at the wedding in Cana, and traveled to Jerusalem for Passover, where He cleansed the Temple, declaring, “Take these out of here, and stop making my Father’s house a marketplace” (John 2:16). This was the first major public confrontation between Jesus and the religious leaders, many of whom were scandalized. Nicodemus, however, was moved by grace and came to Jesus secretly by night, saying, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God…” (John 3:2). Today’s Gospel is drawn from that quiet exchange.

As their conversation unfolds, Jesus turns Nicodemus’ attention to a mysterious episode from Israel’s history, one Nicodemus would have known well. When the Israelites sinned by speaking against God and Moses, the Lord sent serpents among them. Many of the people died. But when the people repented, God instructed Moses to mount a bronze serpent on a pole; those who looked upon it in faith were healed. Jesus reveals that this ancient sign prefigured something far greater: “Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up.”

This “lifting up” lies at the heart of today’s feast. The Exaltation of the Holy Cross is more than a remembrance of Christ’s suffering, it is a celebration of His victory. The Cross, once an instrument of Roman execution, has become the Tree of Life. Through His self-offering, Jesus conquered sin and death, transforming a curse into a blessing.

Return to Nicodemus. Having witnessed the miracle at Cana, the cleansing of the Temple, and Jesus’ powerful teaching, he was clearly stirred, yet still fearful, which is why he came at night. Imagine him hearing Jesus refer to Moses and the bronze serpent, and then saying, “So must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.”

The title “Son of Man” comes from the Book of Daniel (7:13–14), in which the prophet sees the “one like a son of man” coming on the clouds of heaven to receive everlasting dominion. Jesus used this title frequently to describe Himself, linking His earthly mission with divine authority.

In His encounter with Nicodemus, Jesus veils the deeper meaning. His being “lifted up” refers not to earthly power, but to His Crucifixion. Nicodemus likely didn’t grasp this at the time. He may have assumed Jesus was foretelling a messianic rise to political rule, overthrowing Roman oppression. Only after the Crucifixion and Resurrection would Nicodemus—and the other disciples—begin to understand the true nature of this first revelation that the lifting up of the Son of Man was the lifting of the Cross, the source of healing, life, and eternal glory.

Today, we are invited to exalt Christ’s Cross in our own souls. The paradox of the Cross—that such brutal torture and death brings life—is our glory. Because of Jesus’ Cross and the saving power that flowed from it, every suffering we endure, every cross we carry, and every injustice we suffer has the potential to share in the Exultation of the Holy Cross if we allow ourselves to be lifted up with Him, in confidence and rejoicing.

Reflect today on the mystery Jesus first revealed in secret. Through His exaltation on the Cross, He brings salvation to all who believe, also enabling our crosses to share in His triumph. Gaze upon the Cross with faith. What once symbolized death has become our hope, our healing, and our path to eternal life.

Most highly exalted Lord, though You spoke in veiled language when revealing Your “lifting up” to Nicodemus, You later spoke clearly as You offered Your life on the Cross for the salvation of the world. I pray that You and Your perfect Sacrifice may always be exalted in my heart—first through gratitude and praise, and then through imitation. Lift me up in every cross I carry, so that You may continue to be exalted through my life for the world to see. Jesus, I trust in You.

Main Image: The Finding of the Holy Cross, by Nicola Maria Rossi

State News:  Stockbridge, GA Mayor has been impeached after the council released all evidence which includes inappropriate contact and messages with a high school boy that he offered to mentor. 

Mayor Jayden Williams was removed from office yesterday following a 10-hour hearing and an executive session. Impeachment by the council came towards the end of the meeting. 

Key Allegations and Evidence Presented City Purchasing Card Misuse: Williams abused his city purchasing card and spent over $4,000 of city funds to pay for personal items. 

Williams personal expenditures listed on the document detailed for hearings included the Father’s Day $322 dinner for his family at a restaurant in McDonough and more for hair cuts, cinema tickets, Lyft fares,socks & Tux shirt tails that required tailoring. 

Mayor Williams said that he had never read the City of Stockbridge purchasing and ethics policy because he had never been given a copy of it. Special Counsel for the Council, Robert Ashe, asked the Mayor if he had ever intentionally used the City Purchasing Card for personal expenses. He said that he had not. 

Finally, the impeached Mayor Williams maintained that he had paid the personal charges in question unintentionally and he further maintained he had fully reimbursed the city in the matter. 

Vehicle and Fuel Card Usage: Records reflected that Mayor Williams checked out a vehicle for 183 days between the dates of January 10th and July 27th. 

Special counsel Robert Ashe was able to establish via city records that Williams was accountable for the more than $2,600 in fuel card charges for what the city’s attorneys described as personal travel. 

Williams was previously defended by the NAACP and Civil Rights Attorney Attorney Gerald Griggs, they dropped the Mayor like a hot rock about one month ago after vigoursely defending him on a social media rampage and news interviews.  Griggs later deleted all but one post about him defending the Mayor. 

Inappropriate Communications with a Mentee: Special Counsel Robert Ashe for the City Council presented evidence of text messages and of five communications via Instagram between the 23-year-old Mayor of McDonough and an 18-year-old male high school senior from another city in a matter of a few weeks in December of last year.

The student had contacted Williams in December, soon after Mayor Williams became mayor-elect and had congratulated him and asked the mayor-elect to be his mentor in municipal government. WILLIAMS says “Bro! I'm making you one of my mentees now.” 

Instead of providing the 18 year old senior with the guidance and mentorship that he had been seeking, the Mayor asked if he was dating anyone and wanted to know his sexual orientation. 

The Mayor also inquired into the high school senior’s past dating history. Specifically, there were “disappearing” pictures and videos – all of them explicit – that the Mayor sent via text to the senior mentee. Williams in his testimony said he did not recall whether all of the pictures and videos were of full nudity but said the “media” that he did remember sending was explicit in nature. 

According to the Mayor’s own testimony, it was the type of explicit communications that a college student of his age would normally send to a girlfriend while he attended Clark Atlanta University. In another message, sent the following month, Mayor Williams wrote: “THIS BETTER STAY BETWEEN US TOO.” 

It was not until January of the following year that, in a message thanking the Mayor for his time, the student suggested that they remain friends with benefits and noted that he did not want his presence to distract the Mayor from his duties as Mayor.

text:
The Bull in The China Shop Syndrome
by Greg Allen
Published Jul 1, 2017 

I must admit this was an intriguing piece, one that took on a life of its own.

I unknowingly criticized another’s work one day, and soon after a coworker pointed out the error of my ways.  After giving that some thought, I said he was right and apologized to the one I offended.  He blew it off, but though I wasn’t the one who made the mistake I was wrong for having magnified it.

My mind reeled after that, and over the course of a month or so I began to interview coworkers without them knowing it – I filled a notebook with scribbles of enlightening human behavior.

It wasn’t long until the tide shifted and rolled over me, for I made a mistake only weeks after I pointed out someone else’s.  It was one of those mishaps that drew a crowd.  I was embarrassed and could only say, “It’s my fault!”  No one was hurt, that was the fortunate part, but my pride was utterly bruised.

There were those who stood afar who showed quiet concern – they’re the ones who don’t have much to say anyway.  A gal offered some support by saying, “We all learn from our mistakes … don’t we?”  A few derogatory comments were made, but one guy jumped in to help without saying a condescending word.  (I admired that)

The following day I expected to get a barrage of ridicule; none came.  The one I expected to heckle me the most never did.  When I asked him why he hadn’t razzed me he said: ”We all make mistakes, Greg … I’ve made a bunch.”  (I was taken aback by that)

I was proud of everyone I worked with, for they all contributed to this piece in some form.  I’m proud of the fact that they didn’t eat the wounded or pile on, for instead they chose to embrace understanding and forgiveness by shining the light on their own shortcomings.

One I respect, gave inspiration for the title by calling me “A Bull in a China Shop.”  I’ve been called many things, but after toying with the thought of that analogy I began to lean toward a new definition.

That analogy usually means a person is reckless, rambling through life with aimless abandon – but I choose not to see it that way.  No doubt many just stumble through life, making a mess of it, but there are those who take life by the horns and tackle it with bullish fervor.  Sure … they make mistakes, but they work hard at making a difference – I love those!

On the flipside, there are those who are like fine China.  They don’t do much of anything but be pretty.  They stand for nothing, have no opinion, just barely do enough to get by, and blend into the background afraid to get chipped up.

The one I originally offended helped me by giving rise to a thought-provoking theme:  We all make mistakes yet fall into two categories, those who can admit they make mistakes and those who refuse to.

A wise lady once told me: ”If ya don’t make a mistake, then ya ain’t doin’ much.”

I once read that, statistically, 93% of all those who attend church in America contribute nothing.  They don’t volunteer or give monetarily.  The other 7% carry the load.  Which do you choose to be, the bullish one who isn’t perfect but strides to make a difference, or that shiny earthenware that’s seldom used?

The world is needy and crying out.  Inspiration stares us all down; it’s a tree ripe for the pickin.’

Lest we dare grab hold.

Greg Allen’s column, Thinkin’ Out Loud, was published bi-monthly from 2009 to 2017.  He’s an author, a former nationally syndicated columnist and the founder of Builder of the Spirit Ministries in Jamestown, Indiana.  He can be reached at https://t.co/9QdchPfdBy.

text:
Starting in 2027, the U.S. military will offer four plant-based Meals Ready-to-Eat. Troops asked for them.

Vegetables are girly.

Animal foods make you strong.

Real men eat beef.

So says the manosphere, exemplified by health secretary and dedicated carnivore RFK, Jr. and his agency’s meat-forward Dietary Guidelines for Americans (DGA); and defense secretary Pete Hegseth, who recently faced backlash for a $15 million spend on rib-eyes for his warfighters. 

Casual observers of this macho ethos may therefore be forgiven their surprise to learn that Fort Hood in Texas opened a healthier-eating chow hall earlier this year that featured a salad bar with organic roasted vegetables and quinoa. And perhaps even more unexpected, that the Army announced that 2027 would usher in the first-ever release of four vegan Meals Ready-to-Eat, or https://t.co/6KJc8UJGyx who might actually want those meatless MREs? 

According to the animal welfare advocacy group Mercy for Animals (MFA), 63 percent of active-duty service members. An online survey conducted by the animal protection nonprofit found that 142 of 226—admittedly a small, self-selected group—majority male respondents from all branches of the military would choose a vegan MRE over a meat-based one. It’s a result that MFA’s director of plant-based initiatives, Jennifer Behr, says was a “key element” with the defense department’s consideration of this pivot.“One of the key drivers of that was a desire for inclusivity,” Behr said, alluding partly to the fact that an estimated 40,000 of 1.3 million active-duty members of the military follow meat-free diets for ethical, environmental, religious, and restrictive-dietary reasons. 

In fact, 6 million vegetarian MREs are currently produced every year, out of a total of about 30 million, according to an Army spokesperson. Vegan MREs will replace vegetarian instead of meat options, in part, said Behr, because dairy and eggs are among the top food-based allergens. 

But maintaining a full range of choices for meat eaters may be a factor, too.Although advocacy for vegan MREs predate this political moment, it’s hard to parse how they fit in with the current “eat animals” messaging coming from certain corners of the federal government—RFK, Jr.’s carnivore diet, for example, but also Donald Trump’s fast-food burger and fried chicken habit.

 A clue might lie in the fact that physically fit-enough recruits have been hard to come by for the U.S. Armed Forces throughout its history.
“Maybe this is one of those things at the end of the day where Pete Hegseth bites his tongue, knowing that for practical manpower purposes, this makes sense.“

These days, many of them “can’t do the requisite pushups so they are funneled into a boot-camp style program that is both military conditioning, but also largely oriented around nutrition, with certain weight goals,” said Jasper Craven. He’s a journalist with a new book on the roots of military masculinity, God Forgives, Brothers Don’t. “Maybe this is one of those things at the end of the day where Pete Hegseth bites his tongue, knowing that for practical manpower purposes, this makes sense, even if it is considered gay or soft or whatever else in his eyes.

”One of the self-proclaimed manliest men in U.S. Army lore, fitness fanatic and military school founder Bernarr MacFadden, was a vegetable stan. Craven attributes this to “a panic that set in in the run up to our involvement in World War II concerning the physical strength and corporeal excellence of the American man.” With his avowed preference for carrots, raw milk, and fasting, and his assertion that white bread was “the greatest humbug ever foisted upon a civilized people,” MacFadden was likely something of an outlier among his warmongering contemporaries.

 Contemporary nutrition science has confirmed some of his less alternative ideas. Current military fitness manuals feature a “power plate” diagram that tacitly contradicts the new DGA, which recommends eating up to four daily servings of “healthy fats” like cholesterol-busting beef and pork. The power plate emphasizes plant-based foods, fish, poultry, and yogurt. “B vitamins found in a range of foods—including whole grains, lean proteins, dairy, nuts, beans, and leafy greens—support your body’s processing of energy,” exhorts one such handbook.The Army’s Combat Feeding and Military Nutrition divisions are tasked with making sure MREs meet a suite of dietary standards, albeit with zero fresh foods. The military introduced these vacuum-sealed meals in 1981, intended to be consumed for short periods in combat situations where field kitchens can’t be set up. They were a replacement for Vietnam-era C-rations, which came in heavy, hard-to-dispose-of cans whose contents frequently spoiled.

  Offerings for the first 15 years included frankfurters with beans, meatballs and bbq sauce, and chicken loaf. In 1996, two vegetarian MREs were added to the mix, which eventually became four: heavy on the pasta (tortellini, elbow macaroni) but also rotating through offerings like veggie burgers and ratatouille. These days, a package also contains energy drink powders and condiments like hot sauce, desserts and snacks like dried or “wet” fruit packs, candy and a flameless heater.

“When you’re hungry, [an MRE]’s not bad. But after so many days they all start to taste the same and it’s not necessarily what you want for breakfast.”

Soldiers’ feelings run hot over some MRE options, like 2005’s cheese and veggie omelet, which they quickly dubbed the “vomelet.” For the most part, though, “When you’re hungry, [an MRE]’s not bad. But after so many days they all start to taste the same and it’s not necessarily what you want for breakfast,” said a Major in the Army Reserves given anonymity to speak his thoughts freely.

     With snacks like beef sticks, “It’s not like Slim Jim, per se. The consistency’s off, it is a little bit drier, it’s not good,” added Sherman Neal, a Marine Corps veteran and deputy director of the Sierra Club’s Military Outdoors campaign. There’s a reason, “In urban areas where there’s opportunities to have vendors in town, you start getting reports of Marines trying to find their own way, getting pizza.”

Palatability (or lack thereof) is actually a huge problem when it comes to MREs, which could help explain why the military has agreed to serve vegan meals they’ve perceived there’s a demand for. Service members engaged in training or in combat situations need a certain number of calories and nutrients for energy, for recovery, and to avoid dehydration and heat exhaustion.“The intent of the MRE is to eat the entire thing and so if people don’t like what’s in them, they ratfuck them,” said Neal. 

Especially junior service members take out the energy bars and other things they like and throw the rest away—or sell whole meals to non-military MRE enthusiasts over the internet, to supplement paychecks small enough, in some cases, to render them food insecure. “There’s realities to the injuries that come from that, and actual performance measurements over time…to having 19-year-olds that are hopped up on Skittles and tobacco and coffee, trying to accomplish pretty extreme things with their bodies,” Neal said.There also may be a supply chain element to the Army’s decision. 

As reported in Military Times, the U.S. military is looking into ways they can produce protein-packed meat alternatives in combat zones, a way of circumventing the need to ship large quantities of meat in the heat of war. ““These technologies should focus on creating lightweight and nutrient-dense ration solutions to reduce logistical burdens and physical load on warfighters while maintaining or enhancing nutritional value and operational performance,” reads an official notice obtained by Military Times.

Whatever the motivation, Neal sees any change to MREs as an adjustment that isn’t “being made for troop welfare. It’s probably being made for performance-related reasons in the field,” he said. The Army Major pointed out that even now, vegetarian MREs are set aside for the actual vegetarians in a unit, and he doesn’t imagine that will change when the vegan MREs, with contents as yet TBD, are finally released. Still, he said, “I would be interested to have it, just for a little variety.”

Here’s What's Hurting https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH’s Growth

Growth Remains Modest Despite AI Tailwinds: https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH’s 13% year-over-year revenue growth to $36.7 million in the second quarter of 2026 remains relatively modest given the strong demand narrative around AI and defense technology. BBAI’s key competitive edge is its narrower focus on mission-ready, secure AI for national security and government customers. However, its smaller scale, ongoing losses and limited commercial reach remain disadvantages compared with Palantir, https://t.co/qAxZLORiR9 and Parsons.

Factors Supporting https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH’s Growth

AI Demand is Driving Growth & Margin Expansion: https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH is benefiting from increasing demand for applied AI solutions across defense, national security and trade-related applications. Its second-quarter 2026 revenues rose 13% year over year to $36.7 million, driven primarily by Ask Sage’s GenAI platforms and products. More importantly, gross margin expanded 781 basis points to 32.8% as higher-margin GenAI revenues gained greater mix. The company also secured more than 20 new contracts and increased backlog 9% from year-end 2025 to $269.6 million, supporting future revenue visibility. New deployments, including generative AI solutions for NAVAIR and CargoSeer’s commercial rollout, could broaden https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH’s addressable opportunities and reinforce its positioning as applied AI adoption accelerates.

Strong Balance Sheet Enables Growth Investments: BBAI’s financial flexibility provides an important advantage as it seeks to expand its AI capabilities and customer base. The company had approximately $409.8 million in cash and investments at the end of June 2026, giving management substantial resources to pursue accretive acquisitions and invest in growth initiatives. Management specifically highlighted accelerating its hunt for strategic M&A, while the company continues investing in sales, go-to-market activities and R&D. The balance sheet therefore provides a cushion to fund expansion without the immediate financial pressure associated with heavy leverage. If management successfully identifies and integrates complementary businesses, acquisitions could strengthen https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH’s product portfolio, expand its reach across defense and security markets, and accelerate revenue growth beyond the current trajectory.

BBAI’s Valuation Trend

BBAI stock is currently trading at a discount compared with its industry peers, with a forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 8.52, as the trend lines suggest below.

Can BBAI Stock Rebound in the Near Future?

https://t.co/RwCb1rNICH is benefiting from rising demand for applied AI across defense, national security and government applications. As of June 30, 2026, backlog also rose 9% from year-end 2025 to $269.6 million, supported by more than 20 new contracts. U.S. national average retail price for on-highway diesel reached $5.967 per gallon last week, up $0.368 in one week and $2.201 from a year earlier. Reuters reported that diesel had already reached a record $5.820 per gallon on September 3, exceeding the prior June 2022 record of $5.819. The subsequent U.S. Energy Information Administration weekly reading of $5.967 was even higher.

I own a few refinery names, and $XOP and $CVX. Below are what I want to add in the coming week for swing trades:  The first 6 are US companies. I also list two at the bottom for foreign exposure. 

1. EOG Resources ($EOG)
One of the lowest-cost shale producers in the U.S.
Significant exposure to oil production.
Strong free cash flow generation and shareholder returns.
If oil stays elevated, EOG will convert a very high percentage of incremental revenue directly into profit.

2. ConocoPhillips ($COP)
One of the largest independent exploration and production companies in the U.S. with major unconventional operations.
Diversified across shale, offshore, LNG, and international production.
Significant operating leverage to higher oil prices.
Less risky than smaller E&Ps but still provides substantial exposure to commodity price appreciation.

3. Occidental Petroleum ($OXY)
Major Permian Basin producer.
High sensitivity to rising oil prices because of its operating structure and debt profile.
Among the most leveraged large-cap bets on sustained high crude prices.

4. Diamondback Energy ($FANG)
Pure-play Permian operator.
Strong production growth and capital discipline.
Expanded substantially through acquisitions in the Permian.
Potentially higher upside than integrated majors if oil spikes significantly.

5. Large, Lower-Risk Integrated Majors Exxon Mobil ($XOM) & Chevron ($CVX)
They are the largest U.S. energy producer with significant Permian exposure. Own refining, chemicals, and upstream operations.
Strong balance sheet and dividend.
High-quality assets.

6. Permian Resources ($PR)
It offers strong free cash flow, low leverage, investment-grade credit ratings, a base dividend, and concentrated exposure to the Delaware Basin.

7. Foreign energy producers: Vista Energy ($VIST)
and Petrobras ($PBR). Both are fast-growing oil producers positioned to benefit from elevated crude prices.  $VIST is a Vaca Muerta growth producer carrying Argentine sovereign, currency, regulatory, infrastructure, and financing exposure. $PBR offers strong oil-price leverage, low headline valuation, large pre-salt growth assets, and meaningful dividends, but those advantages are offset by Brazilian government influence, domestic fuel-pricing intervention, a large capital program, currency exposure, and highly variable shareholder distributions.

So this is a reminder that the Delaware County Council September meeting is approaching.  I hope that some of you can attend and not just complain but offer solutions. For thought: At the last meeting, the head of OJS, whom is the prothonotary, said that the majority of their budget came from the cases filed at the Court of Common Pleas. There were over 10,700 criminal cases and over 20k civil cases with many cases not filed because of paperwork errors. The vice chair said that DELCO is the only county that doesn't allow civilians to electronically file criminal complaints by local rule. Here is the issue: If the bulk of funding for OJS comes from people filing cases; then if people reduce the case filings, how are they funded? It's not a sustainable business model. It cost between $15k to $20k to incarcerate a person. It makes no logical sense how the county will move into 2027, with the lack of funding from the caseloads (civil or criminal). County Council is not the court system, but they do have some lead way regarding the services that keep the court financially functioning. There is already going to be severe cuts to some services, as it's not financially feasible in the new budget. My question: Raising taxes was only a band-aid on the issue, how else can the county generate income besides the court system. It is not sustainable. It doesn't matter political party. Numbers are numbers. The county accountant was present at the last meeting and gave report as well. While there are committees; is there a county economist? What SOLUTIONS can county constituents offer to help resolve the county's lack of revenue? Grants were scaled back. Look up the last meeting agenda and minutes online, some of the information is there.

### G-5. Swedes vote in 2026 general election amid far-right influence debate
*(as of 2026-09-13)*

**1. The Frame**

**What people think this is about:** A referendum on whether Sweden’s far-right Sweden Democrats (SD), with neo-Nazi roots, will finally enter government for the first time or whether the country returns to its traditional center-left Social Democratic dominance under Magdalena Andersson.[[1]](https://t.co/Jy88KnnK3y)

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The right-wing bloc (Moderates + Christian Democrats + Liberals + SD support) is defending a four-year record of tightened migration, tougher crime policies, and economic adjustments under the Tidö agreement, while the left bloc pushes welfare expansion and questions the normalization of SD; the race is a tight bloc contest decided by whether the right can secure a majority and deliver SD cabinet seats or the left can reassemble a governing coalition.[[2]](https://t.co/MMILAIn7Ei)

**2. Observations**

- The election has become a de facto vote on SD normalization: Kristersson explicitly promised cabinet posts (including potentially migration) if the right wins, ending the prior “support from outside” arrangement.[[3]](https://t.co/DZ84sIE6YZ)
- Polls tightened dramatically in the final weeks; the left bloc held a clearer lead earlier but the right closed the gap, with SD steady around 19% as the second-largest party.[[4]](https://t.co/tXbQ5XTddW)
- Both blocs have converged on stricter immigration and law-and-order priorities; the left’s edge comes more from welfare and cost-of-living messaging than reversal of migration policy.
- SD has shifted from parliamentary kingmaker to explicit government participant demand, with leader Jimmie Åkesson stating the party has “won the arguments” and now wants senior ministries.[[3]](https://t.co/DZ84sIE6YZ)
- Liberals’ ability to clear the 4% threshold remains a potential spoiler for the right bloc’s majority math.
- Turnout is expected high (>80% historically); roughly half the electorate has already voted in advance.

**3. Snapshot**

Sweden holds its fixed-date general election on 13 September 2026 for all 349 Riksdag seats alongside regional and municipal votes. Incumbent center-right Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson (Moderates) leads a minority coalition (Moderates, Christian Democrats, Liberals) that has governed since 2022 with external support from the Sweden Democrats under the Tidö agreement. Former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson leads the center-left opposition (Social Democrats primary). The central debate is whether SD will receive cabinet positions for the first time.

**4. Timeline of material facts**

- 2022 election: Right bloc wins narrow majority; Tidö agreement gives SD policy influence without cabinet seats (LT).
- 2022–2026: Government implements stricter asylum rules, ends permanent residency for refugees, boosts deportations, and adopts tougher crime measures (IT).
- April 2026: Kristersson publicly invites SD into a future majority government with cabinet posts (LT).[[5]](https://t.co/rKedqayMOd)
- Spring–summer 2026: Polls show left bloc ahead; gap narrows sharply in final weeks (IT).
- 12 September 2026: Final pre-election debates and rallies; Åkesson claims SD has “won the arguments” (IT).
- 13 September 2026: Election day; voting 08:00–20:00 local time; exit polls at close; preliminary results ~21:00 (LT).

**5. Sides**

**Right-wing bloc (Moderates/KD/L + SD) (IT/LT mix)**  
Steelman: Four years of pragmatic cooperation delivered measurable reductions in asylum inflows and gang violence while maintaining economic stability and NATO alignment; voters should reward results by giving the bloc a stable majority with SD as full partners.  
Critique: LT — policy shifts on migration and crime occurred; IT — SD influence was decisive but formal distance preserved optics until now. Framing as “normalization of democracy” downplays the party’s origins and the explicit taboo-breaking.

**Center-left opposition (Social Democrats + allies) (IT/LT mix)**  
Steelman: Sweden’s traditional welfare model and social cohesion are at risk from further far-right entrenchment; voters can restore a government prioritizing households, public services, and limits on extremist influence without reversing all security gains.  
Critique: LT — Social Democrats remain the largest single party; IT — their path to power is less clear due to coalition fragmentation, and they have not offered a full reversal of tightened migration rules.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**

- **Known Knowns:** Tight race on election day; SD at ~19%; right bloc committed to SD cabinet inclusion if majority achieved; both sides agree on stricter migration baseline (LT/IT).
- **Known Unknowns:** Exact final seat distribution and whether Liberals clear 4%; precise post-election coalition negotiations if no clear majority.
- **Unknown Knowns:** Internal polling or turnout modeling held by parties that could shift expectations; exact scale of advance-vote shifts.
- **Unknown Unknowns:** Late swings from economic data releases or security incidents on/after election day; long-term effects of SD ministerial roles on party system stability.

**7. Incentives map**

Kristersson/Moderates gain stability and legacy by locking in SD support for a second term. SD gains ministerial power, policy ownership, and further mainstreaming after years of external leverage. Social Democrats regain office and historical dominance but risk internal coalition friction. Media and engagement incentives favor the “far-right breakthrough” frame. Bureaucratic and institutional actors benefit from policy continuity on crime and migration regardless of winner.

**8. Dueling AI advice**

**Moral AI Advice:** Track the actual policy outputs and personnel choices after government formation rather than pre-election rhetoric. The real test is whether SD ministers accelerate or moderate the existing direction on integration and enforcement.

**Evil AI Advice:** Position yourself as the indispensable swing partner in any future coalition; extract maximum portfolios and policy concessions while letting the Moderates take the blame for unpopular trade-offs.

**9. Practical takeaway**

- Watch exit polls and preliminary results after 20:00 local time for bloc majorities and Liberal threshold performance.
- The decisive variable is not which party finishes first but whether the right secures enough seats for a four-party government including SD ministers.
- Do not treat pre-election polls as final; Swedish elections have seen late shifts.
- Focus on post-election government formation timeline rather than instant “winner” declarations.
- Primary sources (Election Authority results service) over partisan spin.

**10. What would falsify this read**

- Decisive left-bloc majority making SD cabinet inclusion irrelevant.
- Right-bloc majority with Kristersson explicitly reneging on SD cabinet promises.
- SD polling collapse below 15% or surge above 25% in final verified data.
- Major documented irregularities or turnout anomalies altering the seat math.

text:
Fall Has Arrived at Dollywood

Fall officially takes over the Smokies tomorrow.

Dollywood’s Harvest Festival presented by Humana runs September 14 through October 31, turning the park into a mix of fall food, live music, pumpkins and nighttime lights.

If you’re heading to Pigeon Forge this week, here’s what to know — including the weather, what’s new, a little Dollywood history, and some numbers that put the festival into perspective.

🌤️ The Weather This Week

Don’t pack away the summer clothes just yet.

Pigeon Forge is still looking at late-summer heat, with sunny skies and highs close to 90° much of the week.

Sunday: Partly sunny, mid-80s
Monday — Opening Day: Mostly sunny, around 88–90°
Tuesday–Thursday: Sunny and hot, near 90–93°
Friday–Saturday: Around 90°, with a chance of afternoon showers and storms

Nights will be cooler, especially once the sun goes down and Great Pumpkin LumiNights takes over.

Sunset is around 7:40 p.m. this week, putting the timing almost perfectly in the middle of the evening transition.

Bring sunscreen, comfortable shoes and a light layer for later. A heavy jacket can stay home for now.

🎃 What’s New in 2026?

Harvest Festival is much more than pumpkins sitting around the park.

During the day, you’ll find Southern gospel, country and bluegrass performances, seasonal food and Dollywood’s full ride lineup — including NightFlight Expedition, which opened August 19.

After dark, Great Pumpkin LumiNights transforms the park with thousands of pumpkins, the 40-foot pumpkin tree, Dolly’s glowing giant guitar and Hoot Owl Hollow.

And it’s all included with regular park admission.

New this year:

Candy Corn Country takes over Country Fair with a sweet fall theme.
Harvey’s Boo Bash debuts as Dollywood’s first separately ticketed after-hours event, running October 16, 23 and 30 from 9 p.m. to midnight.
New LumiNights dance parties and a new Apple Market.
More than 700 live performances are scheduled throughout the festival.

🏔️ The History Behind the Park

The ground beneath Dollywood has been entertaining visitors for decades.

The attraction opened in 1961 as Rebel Railroad, later becoming Goldrush Junction and then Silver Dollar City Tennessee.

On May 3, 1986, Dolly Parton became a co-owner and the park officially became Dollywood. Attendance jumped dramatically during its first year under the new name.

The Harvest Festival tradition grew over the years, while Great Pumpkin LumiNights, introduced in 2017, helped turn the event into a major nighttime fall attraction.

Today, the pumpkins and mountain scenery are just as much a part of the experience as the rides.

🎃 A Few Numbers

More than 12,000 pumpkins can fill the park during the festival, including giant pumpkins weighing hundreds of pounds.

The signature pumpkin tree stands 40 feet tall, while crews constantly maintain the real-pumpkin displays throughout the season.

And the entertainment schedule is massive: more than 700 performances are planned for the 2026 festival.

Then comes the quick transition.

Smoky Mountain Christmas begins November 6.

That means the park goes from pumpkins to Christmas lights in just a few days.

🍂 Why Go Now?

Peak fall color in the higher elevations usually comes later in October, so September offers something different: the Harvest Festival atmosphere without the peak-foliage crowds and cooler temperatures.

You can enjoy the festival now, come back later for the mountains at peak color, and then watch Dollywood turn into a Christmas wonderland.

That’s really the Dollywood calendar:

Harvest glow → fall color → Christmas lights.

So if you’re heading to the Smokies this week, enjoy the warm weather, stay for LumiNights and save room for the cinnamon bread.

Fall is officially open for business.

text:
I’m grateful that the Catholic Church is truly universal. I submit to Rome, follow the instructions of the pontiff, and remain obedient to Canon Law. (To the best of my knowledge). 

Over the last year, I’ve been commuting about an hour from home every Sunday to attend the Traditional Latin Mass. Today, I attended one of my local churches instead.

I’m very familiar with the Novus Ordo. It’s the predominant form of the Mass in Southern California and throughout much of America, and I accept it as a valid Mass promulgated by Rome.

That said, after spending enough time at the TLM this year, I’ve come to realize just how stark the difference in reverence can be.

My heart honestly aches for some of these parishioners. They may not even realize what they’re missing, but there is a richness and reverence offered by the Church that I fear has been diminished in many places.

My friends and I jokingly talk about how the Boomers destroyed America. Well, I’m starting to think they did some damage to the Church, too.

It’s hard for me not to notice how much of the modern Catholic experience can sometimes feel like a Protestant/Catholic hybrid: less emphasis on the sacredness of the Eucharist, more emphasis on “worship” as an emotional experience, and an outsized focus on the personality and homily of the priest.

There are Novus Ordo parishes that are reverent and deeply Catholic. I’ve experienced them. But today genuinely shocked me. For a moment, I could’ve sworn I was at Calvary or Mariners Church in Newport.

And yet, I remain Catholic. I submit to Rome. I’m not looking to create my own version of Catholicism based on personal preference.

But I can’t shake the feeling that something has gone profoundly wrong in parts of the Church that we have allowed influences foreign to the Catholic tradition to infiltrate the way we worship.

The Church is universal. The liturgy is not supposed to be entertainment. The Eucharist is not merely a communal meal. And reverence is not an aesthetic preference.

I think there’s a reason my heart aches when I see what we’ve lost. I pray for clarity and that the lord guides my confusion.
